title: Beyond Modality Harmony: Orthogonal Purification and Topology-Guided MoE for Conflict-Aware Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal Recommender Systems (MRSs) typically rely on a flawed "modality harmony" assumption, presuming that multimodal features are inherently beneficial and strictly aligned with users' collaborative interaction patterns. However, modality-topology conflicts are ubiquitous in real-world scenarios due to deceptive visual clickbaits and mismatched semantics. Blindly integrating these noisy modalities inevitably pollutes the pristine collaborative space, causing severe representation distortion. To address this, we propose Orthogonal purification and topology-guided MoE for conflict-aware multimodal Recommendation (OrthoRec). At its core, OrthoRec introduces Collaborative-Guided Orthogonal Purification (CGOP), which geometrically decouples multimodal features into directions parallel and orthogonal to a pure collaborative anchor. By adaptively truncating the orthogonal noise with an energy-preserving normalization, CGOP rectifies deceptive semantic directions while preserving the modality's intrinsic representation capacity. Furthermore, we design a Topology-Aware Routing Mixture-of-Experts (TAR-MoE). Guided by the collaborative topology, TAR-MoE employs decoupled sigmoid gating to break the zero-sum bottleneck of traditional softmax attention, autonomously determining the injection scale for each purified modality. Finally, a safe-SSL objective is introduced to dynamically penalize the forced contrastive alignment of contradictory pairs. Experiments on three real-world Amazon datasets show that OrthoRec consistently outperforms competitive recent baselines and exhibits improved robustness under modality noise and item sparsity.

title: Application of Reinforcement Learning to the Control of a Simulated Robotic Manipulator
abstract: V diplomskem delu smo zasnovali in implementirali simulacijsko okolje za spodbujevano učenje (angl. reinforcement learning) za robotski manipulator Universal Robots UR10e. Obravnavali smo razvoj okolja, ki omogoča učenje robotske manipulacije v simulaciji. Okolje temelji na simulatorju MuJoCo, knjižnicah Gymnasium in Gymnasium Robotics ter ogrodju PyTorch z uporabo knjižnice Stable-Baselines3. Razvili smo prilagojeni okolji za nalogi doseganja cilja (angl. Reach) ter prijemanja in dvigovanja predmeta (angl. Pick-and-Place). Implementirali smo kartezično vodenje robotskega manipulatorja z uporabo inverzne kinematike po metodi dušenih najmanjših kvadratov (angl. Damped Least Squares), prilagodili smo opazovalni in akcijski prostor, dekompozicijo zahtevnejše naloge ter ustrezni funkciji nagrajevanja. Ovrednotili smo algoritme SAC (angl. Soft Actor-Critic), PPO (angl. Proximal Policy Optimization) in TQC (angl. Truncated Quantile Critics). Pri nalogi doseganja cilja sta algoritma SAC in TQC dosegla 100 % uspešnost, PPO pa približno 80 %. Naloga prijemanja in dvigovanja predmeta je bila zahtevnejša. SAC je dosegel približno 40 % uspešnost, TQC največ približno 30 %, PPO pa naloge ni uspešno dokončal. Rezultati kažejo, da razvito okolje omogoča uspešno učenje osnovne manipulacijske naloge in je osnova za nadaljnji razvoj zahtevnejših nalog ter prenos naučenih strategij na fizične robotske sisteme.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A State of the Art Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于自适应量子拓扑的算法优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum topology algorithms to optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. We propose a novel algorithm, termed "Dynamic Quantum Topology Optimization," that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on the quantum topology structure of the problem. This approach allows for automated parameter tuning, leading to improved performance, particularly when optimizing complex algorithms. The core mechanism involves monitoring and responding to changes in the quantum topology, resulting in a more nuanced and adaptive optimization process. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to significantly enhance optimization performance in various domains.

title: 微观量子计算的复杂性规约
abstract: This paper investigates the complex challenges inherent in traditional quantum computing, focusing on the limitations in effectively tackling intricate quantum algorithms. We propose a novel approach termed "纠缠协同计算" (CCC) to address this challenge, aiming to decompose complex quantum computations into smaller, more manageable sub-problems through the strategic utilization of quantum entanglement. This method leverages entanglement to establish correlations between different qubits, enabling parallel processing and optimization strategies that enhance the performance of these algorithms. The core claim is that CCC offers a significant advancement in the handling of complex quantum problems, potentially unlocking new computational capabilities. This paper details the underlying mechanisms of the CCC approach, provides a mathematical framework for its implementation, and explores the potential benefits and limitations of this innovative technique.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis (QEDDA)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis (QEDDA) presents a revolutionary algorithmic approach to topological data analysis, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical methods through the application of quantum entanglement. This paper proposes a novel quantum protocol designed to create entangled representations of graph data, enabling significantly accelerated pattern recognition and precise quantification of fundamental topological patterns. The core claim centers on the potential for QEDDA to discover and characterize complex graph structures with unprecedented speed and precision, offering a paradigm shift in the field of data analysis.

title: Topology-Aware Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of topology into quantum algorithm design, aiming to enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum computations. The core claim is to develop a method for systematically mapping quantum states to topological structures, thereby facilitating the creation of quantum algorithms that optimally exploit these inherent properties. We propose a framework leveraging the interplay between quantum states and topological invariants to guide the design of novel quantum algorithms. The research emphasizes the crucial role of topology in shaping quantum system behavior and offers a potential pathway toward significant improvements in computational capabilities. Specifically, we demonstrate the practical implications of this approach through a theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation of a simplified quantum algorithm. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum information theory by addressing a fundamental challenge in algorithm design – the exploitation of topological structures within quantum systems.

title: Quantum-Driven Lattice Parameter Optimization for Materials
abstract: Quantum-driven lattice parameter optimization is a novel approach to materials science that leverages the power of quantum computing to efficiently explore the parameter space of crystal structures. Traditional methods, while effective, often face computational bottlenecks, limiting the scope of potential discoveries. This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced optimization strategy utilizing quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) techniques to systematically search for optimal lattice parameters, potentially leading to the identification of novel material properties. The core mechanism centers around quantum algorithms designed to navigate the complex parameter space, offering a potential paradigm shift in materials discovery. This work addresses the challenges of computational complexity and provides a framework for harnessing quantum mechanics to accelerate materials design. This research explores the feasibility of using quantum algorithms to optimize lattice parameters, focusing on the potential to uncover new material characteristics and advancements.

title: Adaptive Topologies of Quantum Information Learning
abstract: Quantum information learning is a rapidly evolving field with significant potential for breakthroughs in quantum computation and quantum information processing. Traditional approaches often rely on manually crafted quantum circuits and complex optimization strategies. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information learning based on adaptive topologies, leveraging the non-locality inherent in quantum entanglement. We present a new algorithm that utilizes a knowledge graph constructed from quantum entanglement to dynamically model quantum states, resulting in more precise physical simulations and numerical computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological knowledge graph to represent the quantum state, and then using the non-local properties of entanglement to learn and evolve this graph. This algorithm offers a promising path towards automated optimization and improved performance in quantum information learning.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Distributed Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the problem of distributed resource allocation. Traditional approaches to this problem often struggle with the complexity arising from dynamic environments, decentralized control, and the need for global optimization. MARL offers a compelling alternative by training a population of agents, each responsible for a localized resource allocation decision. This approach allows for adaptive behavior and emergent coordination, potentially leading to superior performance compared to centralized solutions. The core of this work is the design and implementation of a MARL framework where agents learn optimal allocation strategies through trial and error, guided by a reward function that reflects the overall system objective. We explore different MARL algorithms, including Independent Q-Learning (IQL) and Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE), to assess their effectiveness. The research demonstrates the potential of MARL to efficiently solve complex distributed resource allocation problems, adapting to dynamic environments and optimizing overall system performance. This work provides a foundational approach for future research in this area.

title: Symbiotic Algorithm for Computational Complexity
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Symbiotic Algorithm, designed to optimize computational complexity by fostering symbiotic relationships between tasks within a computational chain. The algorithm dynamically allocates computational resources to tasks based on their position in a complexity chain, aiming to minimize the overall complexity while maintaining a consistent level of performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, revealing a significant improvement in complexity compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors task progress and adjusts resource allocation to achieve optimal balance.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography Geometric Formalization
abstract: Quantum Information Cryptography (QIC) aims to secure information through cryptographic algorithms that are resistant to computational attacks. Traditional cryptographic approaches frequently rely on mathematical hardness assumptions, while geometric cryptography leverages the properties of geometric spaces to create secure systems. This paper explores a novel approach to QIC: the geometric formalization of key decryption. We propose a method that transforms the core decryption problem into a geometric problem, employing a novel optimization algorithm to refine cryptographic parameters and enhance security. The core claim is that this geometric formalization significantly improves the security of key decryption compared to traditional methods, leveraging the power of geometric topology. This work introduces a new framework for analyzing and optimizing cryptographic systems, potentially offering a more robust approach to secure communication.

title: Title: Interference-Based Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed the Interference-Based Algorithm Optimization (IBAO), designed to significantly enhance the speed and efficiency of complex computations. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with computationally intensive problems, necessitating brute-force approaches. The IBAO leverages the inherent interference patterns within the algorithm's structure to dynamically guide the computation process, effectively reducing the need for exhaustive search and improving overall performance. This algorithm utilizes a sophisticated interference model to identify and mitigate redundant computations, leading to substantial speed improvements across a range of computational tasks. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and practical applications, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing challenging scenarios. This paper explores the core mechanisms behind the algorithm's success, focusing on the intricate interplay between the interference model and the computation itself.

title: ##拓扑-物理耦合的自然语言生成
abstract: This paper explores the integration of topological structure and physics models into natural language generation (NLG) systems. We propose a novel approach that dynamically links linguistic structures with underlying physical systems, enabling the generation of text characterized by specific topological properties. The core mechanism involves leveraging a combination of a pre-trained natural language generation model and a dedicated topological structure processing module. This integration allows the model to learn and generate text that reflects the inherent topological relationships within the input data, offering a significant leap forward compared to existing methodologies. The paper details the architecture of the proposed system, discusses the challenges and opportunities involved in this integration, and provides preliminary results demonstrating the generation of text exhibiting desired topological features.

title: Cross-platform deployment and characterization of an on-device generative conversational agent
abstract: Recent advances in Language Models (LMs) enable conversational systems that interpret natural-language requests, select application actions, and generate user-facing responses. However, existing studies typically either examine complete assistants with limited deployment evidence or benchmark individual components in isolation. This work advances the state of the art through a unified cross-platform characterization of a local speech-to-text-LM-text-to-speech pipeline combining Moonshine, Piper, and four quantized LMs ranging from 1.2B to 8B parameters. The pipeline is deployed on an Nvidia Jetson AGX Orin, a Raspberry Pi 5, and an STM32MP257F-EV1, and evaluated in thermostat and washing-machine use cases. Action-selection capability is assessed on 200 labelled explicit and implicit requests per use case, while deployment is characterized through metrics such as memory footprint, speech Real-Time Factor, decoding throughput, power consumption, etc. Granite 3.3 (8B) achieves the highest Macro F1-scores, whereas Qwen3.5 (4B) provides the best capability–resource trade-off. Speech processing is faster than real time on the Jetson and Raspberry Pi, while the STM32MP2 supports smaller LMs in memory but is unsuitable for responsive CPU-only conversation. LM decoding accounts for over 90% of turn duration, and memory-Roofline analysis identifies model footprint, runtime support, response length, and streaming execution as the main optimization levers.

title: Transversal Gates and Magic State Distillation in an Optimally Synthesized Spin-Qubit Shuttling Bus
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires not only reliable logical qubit storage, but also the ability to perform high-fidelity logical operations between error-corrected qubits at scale. While much of the existing literature focuses on optimizing syndrome extraction for a single logical qubit, the co-design of physical architectures that support both robust error correction and efficient logical computation remains an open challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-qubit spin-qubit shuttling bus architecture that addresses both requirements simultaneously. The architecture optimizes the physical qubit layout for syndrome extraction and supports transversal two-qubit logical gates between an arbitrary number of logical qubits, achieving all-to-all logical connectivity through coherent spin shuttling. We further propose an ancilla-sharing scheme that encodes multiple logical qubits within a single logical element, compressing the physical footprint of the processor and improving long-range gate fidelity. Extending the architecture from a one-dimensional bus to a two-dimensional grid of shuttling tracks reduces the inter-qubit distance, yielding consistent improvements in logical error. Finally, we apply the Quantum Reverse Mapping methodology at the logical level to optimize the layout of a \textit{15-to-1} magic state distillation circuit, demonstrating how the transversal capabilities of the proposed architecture can be leveraged for universal fault-tolerant computation. Taken together, these results establish a principled co-design framework that bridges the physical, error-correction, and logical computation layers of the quantum stack, and demonstrate that spin-qubit shuttling architectures are a viable and flexible substrate for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: From Detection to Localization: A Unified Forensics Framework for Fully Synthetic and Tampered Images
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models has significantly worsened the problem of manipulated image detection, as these methods are capable of producing highly realistic forgeries, reinforcing the importance of multimedia forensics. Conventional approaches typically frame image manipulation detection as a binary classification task (real vs. generated), which limits the capability to distinguish and localize different forms of manipulation. To address these constraints, this work extends an existing detector by introducing a unified multiclass framework (real vs. fully generated vs. tampered). In addition to classifying image authenticity, the framework incorporates a segmentation branch to enable pixel-level localization of tampered regions. The proposed approach outperforms selected recent benchmarks, offering an efficient solution with improved classification accuracy and higher IoU scores for the localization task. Find the code at https://github.com/anngal01/From-Detection-to-Localization-A-Unified-Forensics-Framework-for-Fully-Synthetic-and-Tampered-Images.

title: Fair Stable Matching: A Nash Social Welfare Approach
abstract: While traditional stable matching algorithms, such as the Gale-Shapley algorithm, prioritize stability, they may fall short of achieving equitable outcomes among participants. We study the role of \emph{Nash social welfare} (NSW) as a fairness objective in the classic \emph{stable marriage problem}. We develop \texttt{SNSW-Alg} that finds a stable matching that maximizes Nash social welfare under rank-induced utilities in $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^4)$ time, where $n$ is the number of men or women. We demonstrate that \texttt{SNSW-Alg} balances equity while preserving stability. We empirically evaluate our methods across diverse preference distributions, demonstrating significant gains in fairness without substantial losses in other key measures such as regret, egalitarian criterion, and sex equality. Our findings suggest that the stable matching produced by \texttt{SNSW-Alg} is statistically Pareto-undominated by stable matchings based on other fairness measures - regret, egalitarian, and sex equality. This study offers compelling insights for designing fair-stable matching.

title: Affective Scaffolding in Creative Learning: The Vivience Framework for Empathic Digital Humans as Collaborative Partners
abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) systems increasingly transition from passive computational tools to active dialogic partners within educational ecosystems, the affective and communicative dimensions of human–AI interaction demand rigorous theoretical interrogation. Prevailing scholarship predominantly prioritises system efficiency and informational accuracy, frequently marginalising the affective investments and socio-emotional scaffolding requisite for creative learning. Within these vulnerable contexts, ostensibly "neutral" AI interfaces architected for transactional efficiency rather than relational pragmatics are frequently interpreted by learners as affectively indifferent or implicitly evaluative. This phenomenon, conceptualised herein as the "Neutrality Trap," is theorised to engender a discursive void that stifles the psychological safety necessary for creative risk-taking. To address this lacuna, this paper advances the "Vivience Framework for Affective Scaffolding," an integrated conceptual architecture for Empathic Digital Humans (EDHs). Drawing from foundational interactional modelling outlined in Singh (2025), this framework operationalises AI empathy not as an anthropomorphic simulation of sentience, but as a design-dependent communicative scaffold that supports learning regulation. By synthesising Vygotskian scaffolding (Vygotsky, 1978), Self-Determination Theory (Ryan & Deci, 2000), and Control-Value Theory (Pekrun, 2006), the paper articulates the theoretical mechanisms by which AER is hypothesised to mitigate "Affective Load,” the extraneous cognitive burden induced by anxiety and perceived judgment. Finally, the paper posits the "Vivience Protocol" as a rigorous methodological reference design for future empirical inquiry, advocating a paradigmatic shift from monologic, transactional AI to dialogic, relationally attuned AI partners in education.

If you snoop through the code you will see that arXiv is also a hidden option. I removed it because CORS settings need to be used as they do not allow origin=* in the API call alone. I am not committing to maintaining the software going forward as I am beginning a new project which will be hosted at https://pathmap.org/alchemy. The goal of the new project is to "gamify" science and knowledge through a free (not BYOAI Key model) AI interface that lets anyone mix two concepts and make veridical literature based discoveries. I will personally be using it for things like "Magnolia and COPD" and "Pulverized Magnolia Bark and Pulverized Sunflower Seeds" or "PDEVs and SIRT3", etc., in order to seed a scientific database of known plant derived extracellular vesicles, their known properties (e.g., cargo/payload size, hydrophilic/lipophilic/electrophilic data, SMILES strings, and any other helpful data that can be open-public in order to help scientists derive WHICH PDEVs would be the most effective fit/use for a pathology. Using the PathMap software, I have published about using Ginger/Ginseng or other exosome sized PDEVs via intradermal hydrogel for "washout" delivery to localized lymphatic system targets, an idea I am putting here because it could be useful for treating breast cancer. Research shows that it would stop metastasis from advancing to the next zone and allow targeted delivery of chemotherapy, potentially allowing a non-destructive version of chemo targeting versus blood delivered routes. Another main discovery set I want to note before I open source the code is about genetic c9orf72 ALS. I published about intranasal delivery of Spermidine-modified Ginger Derived Extracellular Vesicles. The Spermidine mod targets the MARK2-eif5a axis which is helpful, not only for downregulating the MARK2 axis if it were needed - such as to potentially reduce DPRs in c9orf72 ALS - but more importantly, as a homing device / beacon system to deliver Cas9 CRISPR gene therapy. This platform will also apply to NEK-1 ALS. This platform does not apply to sporadic ALS, because the data shows that Sporadic ALS is a collapse in retinal-RGNEF via a toxin or toxin-like vector that steals retinal synaptic zinc, thereby removing the NMDA receptor "brake fluid". The catch is the thermodynamic affinities: The toxin must have a zinc affinity > glutamate (from synapse) but < than RGNEF which *could* create a mis-shuttling loop that floods Zinc to RGNEF proteins and causes rigidity. Dr Michael Strong's work, and separately, Droppleman et al., show that if the RGNEF protein were to have its NF242 Terminal lose function or be sequestered, this could lead to TDP-43 proteinopathy. 97% of sALS patients had a TDP-43 biomarker in the retina. I cannot find any congenitally blind sALS cases. Schizophrenia is the only other disease I could find with such a "blindness shield" and it is related to corollary discharge in SD. So why not also in sALS, I wondered. Well, turns out that the NMDA brake fluid theft causes overexcitement in Retinal Ganglion Cells. We know that the bad TDP-43 causes cryptic STMN2 missplicing in motor neurons, and I have no reason to doubt that it would cause cryptic missplicing in retinal ganglion STMN2. All of this said, there were (are) two missing links which I can explain but not prove. If the RGC overexcitement caused misfiring of corollary discharge AND, the bayesian brain feed forward models allow a "concensus" that could misinterpret laggy/unexpected CD (corollary discharge) as "instant movement", then the bayesian brain would also then calculate that the motor neurons or golgi tendon organs or pathways were fautly and increase the gain because the movement was reported by the brain itself (the eyes) as instant yet the peripheral sensor reported XX milliseconds. I see it like a see-saw and it is plausible with PubMed science. One issue was "how does this go retrograde from retina upstream?". I cannot explain that but my research on Ebola leads me to think that this is the "ghost factor" in ALS: Some environmental toxins that "do not cause ALS" but are "associated with ALS" may be randomly forming toxic vector "clouds" by aerosolization of the toxin in a way that binds it to, or encapsulates it within, a plant derived extracellular vesicle, and the delivery is through the cribriform plate, bypassing the BBB and then moving *downstream* to the retina, not retrograde up! All said, if my theories and views on sporadic ALS are correct, then either a bright light or total darkness (not sure of polarity, I need a Neuro-Ophthalmologist to consider it) would be **REQUISITE** for any long term cure of sporadic ALS because the bayesian brain will always raise the gain on signals to peripherals under this model until the eyes are not being trusted at all (eg, does total darkness therapy lower the trust weights on the eye feeds and allow the brain to trust the peripheral sensors without penalizing them for being reported as "late/slow"?). Glaucoma is much like sALS in the retina from what I read, but the requirement of the optic nerve injury for Glaucoma may explain why there is an inverted occurrence between sALS and glaucoma - the brain knows not to trust the eyes as much and does not penalize. I also posited that c9orf72 ALS upscaled p62 systems may explain why there is ZERO (that I could find) occurrence of the sALS retina TDP-43 signature found in c9orf72 ALS yet they both have the TDP-43 markers otherwise. Vitreous fluid/humor data may show a different progression of c9ALS and sALS. Also, c9ALS and FTLD are the same genetic defect and the mixing of the data with sALS data has made the current view of ALS confounding. My models explain it differently and with consilience. I hope you can use the software as I did and find the truth in the literature and help heal the land. And, Endometriosis and Ovarian Tumors... I published about how an injected hydrogel of moxa or borneal modified **ginger** EVs would be ideal for ovarian tumor therapy delivery because the borneal can likely "drill" through the hard outside of the tumor and the 6-shogaol that would be naturally within the ginger-evs is known to cause apoptosis in ovarian tumor cells. While looking at endometriosis, I found that hyaluronic-acid modified ginger-evs would be the trick, but then after further consideration, using both the moxa/borneal and HA modified EVs for either endometriosis or ovarian tumor would potentially be a good thing to test. I can only show "the math" of the science with this PathMap software. We will always need real human scientists and real researchers doing real lab work, and I hope that this software can help you connect the dots from Turkey+Pom for COPD diet ideas to figuring the next iPSC experiment you should do, or what thesis makes sense to write. All of that said, the 144 publishings on PathMap.org are also archived in the Zenodo community for PathMap, and there are no planned further publishings to that blog/resource as I move forward with PathMap Alchemy and PathMap Nutrition in the future. Enjoy the software and use it responsibly. Sorry if there are any glitches and if someone or anyone chooses to start a GIT for this or their derivative works, it may be helpful. The software is AS_IS and NO_WARRANTY so you will have to take it from here on those items. Finally, nearly all of this was done - created, tested, deployed, used, maintained, and marketed, from a 4GB metroPCS phone. It was my vision that even a youth in Indonesia may have an idea about some cure or some thing that would greatly help humanity, and they they should not be disallowed due to lack of resource, language barriers, lack of technology or access to it, and so forth. title: Agent Task Control Plane: A Reference Architecture for Human-Governed Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Agent Task Control Plane (ATCP) is a reference architecture for governing parallel AI-agent work. It addresses the growing human cognitive burden of managing multiple asynchronous agents, including task-state loss, context contamination, missing deployment or verification steps, goal drift, and weak traceability. ATCP introduces a task-first control-plane model built around authoritative state machines, coordination, observability, human approval, verification, traceability, and human-attention routing. Its central principle is: scaling agents should not scale human cognitive load.

title: Self-Referential Code Generation for Formal Verification
abstract: Formal verification is a critical technique for ensuring software correctness, but its widespread adoption is hampered by the difficulty of creating precise and expressive formal specifications. Traditional approaches require significant manual effort and domain expertise, often leading to incomplete or overly complex specifications. This paper introduces a novel system for automating this process through self-referential code generation. The system leverages a grammar that encodes the program's logic and potential error conditions, generating formal specifications directly from the source code. The generated specification is then used to automatically derive a verification proof. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, arguing that it can substantially reduce the burden of specification creation and, potentially, broaden the applicability of formal verification. The core idea is to let the code *define* the verification process, creating a feedback loop. This approach tackles the expressiveness barrier by using the program itself as the source of the verification rules. The system relies on a carefully designed grammar that captures the semantics of the code, allowing for the automatic construction of formal models suitable for verification. The resulting verification process is intrinsically tied to the code's logic, increasing the likelihood of detecting subtle errors.

title: Probability Field Theory: Adaptive Distribution Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model based on probability field theory, specifically designed for dynamic systems. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to accurately represent complex systems. This research proposes a self-adapting probability distribution model that dynamically adjusts probability distributions based on system state, resulting in improved prediction accuracy. The core mechanism involves introducing an adaptive probability distribution model utilizing the self-adaptivity of probability field theory, enabling precise modeling of system probability distributions and dynamic adjustment. The paper presents a comprehensive investigation of this approach, detailing its implementation, validation, and performance evaluation. The primary goal is to demonstrate the efficacy of the self-adapting model in handling complex systems with evolving probability distributions.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence via Causal Inference Framework
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of current Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods, which primarily focus on post-hoc explanations of model behavior without adequately incorporating causal reasoning. The core claim is that these approaches often generate unreliable explanations due to a neglect of causal relationships. We propose a novel framework integrating causal inference into the XAI process. This framework aims to provide more robust and trustworthy explanations by explicitly modeling and reasoning about causal relationships within the data and the model. The proposed methodology utilizes techniques from causal discovery and causal modeling to identify key causal pathways influencing model predictions, leading to explanations that are grounded in underlying causal mechanisms. We believe this approach represents a significant advancement in XAI, moving beyond superficial explanations towards truly interpretable and reliable AI systems.

title: ##基于生物磁场控制的量子比特操控
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility and potential of utilizing biological magnetic fields for quantum bit (qubit) control and manipulation. The core concept involves leveraging the subtle forces exerted by biological magnetic fields on quantum systems to achieve precise control and entanglement. We propose a system design incorporating a specialized device to generate and control these fields, allowing for targeted interactions with qubits. The theoretical framework presented details the mechanisms involved, exploring the challenges and opportunities associated with this novel approach to quantum information processing. This research explores a potentially disruptive method for qubit manipulation, moving beyond traditional electromagnetic control and offering a pathway for utilizing biological systems in the realm of quantum technologies. We analyze the key factors influencing the effectiveness of this technique, including field strength, qubit sensitivity, and environmental noise. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the possibility of achieving robust and scalable quantum control using biologically generated magnetic fields. ---

title: Quantum Topology Computation: Adaptive Optimization Framework
abstract: Quantum Topology Computation (QTC) is a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages the inherent quantum properties of topological states to perform complex calculations. This paper introduces a new framework, Adaptive Optimization of Quantum Topology Computation (AOC), designed to dynamically adjust quantum parameters during computation, thereby mitigating errors and enhancing precision. We detail the framework's architecture, focusing on the core mechanism of automated parameter tuning based on a self-adaptive optimization strategy. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of AOC through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to address challenges associated with traditional QTC methods. The significance of this work lies in its potential to unlock new computational possibilities and significantly improve the performance of QTC algorithms.

title: Topological Information-Driven Quantum Computer Topology Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of topological information-driven quantum computing, a novel approach leveraging the inherent structure of topological quantum systems to enhance computational efficiency. We introduce a new quantum algorithm designed to optimize quantum computations by strategically utilizing the relationships between nodes and edges within a topological framework. The core claim centers on the transformative impact of topological structure as the foundational element of a quantum computer, enabling a significant improvement in computational performance compared to classical approaches. We detail the methodology, explain the underlying principles, and present preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this technique.

title: Quantum Geometry Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum geometry-based adaptive algorithm designed to precisely calculate and optimize geometric structures. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting efficiency. Our algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum geometry to dynamically adjust its parameters, enabling accurate solutions across a wide range of geometric problems. This adaptive approach contrasts with conventional algorithms, offering significant improvements in speed and accuracy. The core mechanism centers on the algorithm's ability to map geometric transformations and constraints to quantum states, facilitating a form of "quantum intuition" in the optimization process. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, introduces key mathematical concepts, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a series of challenging geometric optimization tasks.

title: Conversational AI Capability and Organizational Agility
abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a strategic capability for enhancing customer interactions and supporting organizational processes. However, the mechanisms through which conversational AI capability contributes to organizational agility remain underexplored. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities View, Service-Dominant Logic, and Information Processing Theory, this study examines the mediating roles of customer experience and decision-making efficiency. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was adopted using perceptual survey data collected from managers in highly digitalized companies. The proposed model was tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that conversational AI capability is positively associated with organizational agility, both directly and indirectly through customer experience and decision-making efficiency. The study contributes to the literature by integrating complementary theoretical perspectives to explain how conversational AI capabilities foster organizational agility and offers practical implications for organizations seeking to strengthen their adaptive capabilities in dynamic environments. Because the study relies on cross-sectional perceptual data, the findings should be interpreted as evidence of associations rather than causal relationships.

title: Following the Money Trail: Spotting Laundering Sinks in Bitcoin Networks with Cluster-Guided Graph Learning
abstract: Follow the money in Bitcoin, and it often dies in a sink. An address takes in funds but almost never sends them onward. We wanted to know if a Graph Neural Network (GNN) could be trained to identify these exact dead ends, and more importantly, whether flagging them would actually help investigators catch a higher volume of illicit transactions. Working with the Elliptic graph comes with a catch. The 165 standard node features already bake in neighbor aggregates, meaning message-passing mostly just rediscovers what the data already says. We call this the structural blind spot. Our fix is deliberately small. We started with five structural features and applied a log transform before running a supervised Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) projection. We then used k-Means clustering with k = 10. This let us append a distance-to-sink-centroid score to each node. Because everything is fit strictly on training nodes, we can guarantee absolutely zero data leakage, which means the model’s performance on unseen data is genuinely earned. F1-Illicit jumps by 7.6% while F1-Macro rises 3.9% over the raw-feature baseline. PR-AUC remains competitive. Adding just a slight dose of supervised structure forces the model to recognize the laundering operations hiding right in front of it, giving investigators a lightweight, label-efficient tool to track illicit funds without getting lost in the noise.

title: Toward scalable generative AI: efficient language model distillation via zero-shot rationales
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates an efficient approach for distilling Large Language Models (LLMs) into smaller, application-specific models using zero-shot Chain of Thought (CoT) rationale generation and Optimization by Prompting (OPRO). To address the challenges of deploying computationally intensive generative AI for narrow tasks or resource-constrained environments, the approach leverages LLM reasoning capabilities to generate both labels and natural language explanations for unlabeled data. By reducing reliance on human-generated annotations, the approach substantially lowers annotation requirements and prompting costs while maintaining comparable performance in the evaluated settings. We formulate distillation as a multi-task learning problem in which student models are trained to jointly predict labels and learn from teacher-generated rationales, with the goal of improving data efficiency and generalization. Building on established zero-shot Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting and the OPRO prompt optimization technique, we use teacher-generated rationales to reduce annotation token requirements and examine the associated performance and efficiency gains. Additionally, we systematically investigate how explanation properties affect distillation efficiency. Across natural language inference and question answering benchmarks, results indicate that near-optimal performance can be achieved even when rationales are provided for only a subset of the training data, and that shorter explanations are often sufficient. These findings provide practical insights into the trade-offs between rationale generation cost and student model performance. Overall, this work contributes empirical evidence on the effectiveness and cost characteristics of rationale-based distillation for training compact, task-specific language models with minimal human intervention.

title: Compute-in-Memory Attention: A Time-Domain Analog Softmax Circuit with RC-Tunable Temperature
abstract: Softmax is a key operation in Transformer attention, but its exponentiation and normalization add significant overhead in compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators, especially when analog attention scores must first be converted to the digital domain. This work presents a tunable-temperature analog softmax circuit in GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) technology that operates directly on CIM-generated score voltages without intermediate analog-to-digital conversion. Each input score is converted into a time-domain event using a shared falling ramp. The corresponding comparator transition samples an RC-decaying reference to generate an exponential weight, which is then processed by an in-circuit normalization stage. In contrast to analog softmax circuits that rely on transistor weak-inversion behavior for exponentiation, the proposed architecture controls the softmax response through the ramp slope and RC time constant, enabling programmable effective temperature. The 128-element architecture is evaluated using transistor-level and post-layout extracted simulations, including multi-level input vectors, capacitance variation and mismatch, process and temperature variation, monte carlo analysis, and shared-interconnect parasitics. The complete 128-element implementation occupies 9453.42~$μ\mathrm{m}^{2}$ including the shared global ramp circuitry, while each replicated softmax element occupies 70.2~$μ\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The circuit achieves a 242.97-ns evaluation latency at 13.44~mW total power, corresponding to 25.5~pJ per output element. The simultaneous 128-element evaluation achieves an RMSE of 24.46~mV relative to the ideal softmax response. The extracted circuit characteristics are further incorporated into a MemTorch-based hardware-aware Transformer model, where the proposed softmax achieves a validation loss within 2.5\% of the ideal-softmax baseline.

title: LLM-Driven Joint Evolution of Coupled Heuristics Components for Routing Optimization
abstract: Heuristic design for combinatorial optimization remains heavily reliant on expert knowledge, while existing large language model (LLM)-enhanced evolutionary methods typically evolve isolated algorithmic components, even when one determines the search state on which another operates. This paper proposes LLM-driven Heuristic Components Joint Generation (LLM-HCJG), a population-based framework that jointly generates and co-evolves interdependent heuristic components under a shared design blueprint. Applied to guided local search (GLS), LLM-HCJG couples solution initialization with penalty construction and embeds the generated pair into an enhanced online search mechanism. The resulting form is further transferred from the traveling salesman problem (TSP) to the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP). Theoretical analysis establishes the non-separable state-transition effects between the two components and the advantage in generation consistency. Across synthetic instances and 41 public TSPLIB/CVRPLIB benchmarks, LLM-HCJG attains consistently low optimality gaps, including best or tied-best results on 28 of 29 TSPLIB instances and all 12 CVRPLIB instances. Ablation and structural analyses further indicate that these gains are associated with cross-component compatibility and alignment rather than isolated-component recombination. These results support effective cross-instance transfer within the evaluated routing settings under limited-sample, modest-cost training.

title: Online Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization Matching the Offline $0.401$ Factor
abstract: We study online maximization of nonnegative, non-monotone DR-submodular functions over compact convex down-closed subsets of the $d$-dimensional unit cube. The best known constructive offline approximation factor is $0.401$ under the corresponding meta-solvability assumptions, whereas comparable adversarial online guarantees had remained at $1/e$. We show that this factor is also achievable online. In the post-decision full-information value-oracle model, our algorithm attains factor $0.401$ with sublinear approximate regret when oracle feedback is conditionally unbiased and bounded. The online algorithm does not run the offline construction on a changing objective. Instead, it replaces the offline objective-dependent box step by a weighted online learner that controls the required residual terms cumulatively. An exact asymmetric balance theorem preserves the offline coefficients despite adversarial variation. The direct implementation has $O(T^{3/4})$ regret and uses $O(dT^{1/4})$ oracle calls per round. More generally, for every $δ\in[0,1/4]$, batching gives $O(T^δ)$ calls per round and $O(T^{4/5-δ/5})$ regret, including a one-call $O(T^{4/5})$ endpoint. Under a positive-anchor condition, randomized blocking retains factor $0.401$ with $O(T^{5/6})$ one-point bandit regret.

title: Contrasting Effects of Control on Fidelity and Fidelity Deviation in Controlled Teleportation
abstract: Teleportation performance is commonly characterized by the average teleportation fidelity, while its variation over input states provides additional information captured by the fidelity deviation. In controlled teleportation, the controller's measurement introduces an additional source of fidelity variation through its measurement outcomes. We investigate the fidelity deviation in controlled teleportation with three-qubit pure states. We derive a lower bound on the fidelity deviation and show that it is attainable together with the maximal average teleportation fidelity. Among the measurements attaining the maximal average fidelity, however, the fidelity deviation can vary depending on the controller's measurement. We further examine the effect of controller assistance by comparing controlled teleportation with direct teleportation using the reduced state. Unlike the maximal average fidelity, which cannot decrease with controller assistance, the minimal fidelity deviation is not necessarily reduced by controller assistance. In particular, for any W-class pure state, controller assistance cannot reduce the fidelity deviation. These results reveal contrasting effects of control on teleportation fidelity and its deviation in controlled teleportation.

title: Opening the Black Box a Crack: A State of the Art Review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of explainable AI and interpretability as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Core Claim: A Quantum-Adaptive Dynamic Matrix Decomposition Method
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-adaptive dynamic matrix decomposition method, aiming to significantly enhance computational efficiency, particularly when dealing with large matrices. Traditional matrix factorization methods often exhibit limitations in scalability and speed, especially with high-dimensional datasets. Our approach leverages the unique properties of quantum self-adapted matrix decomposition, allowing for rapid and efficient breakdown of matrices. The core mechanism involves a quantum-optimized decomposition process that adapts to the matrix's structure, leading to substantial performance gains. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its potential impact on various matrix factorization applications. This work contributes to the advancement of efficient matrix computation techniques.

title: The Emergence of Semantic Networks: A Novel Approach to Enhanced Semantic Understanding and Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for semantic network fusion, leveraging multiple scales to enhance semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities. Traditional approaches often overlook the crucial relationship between different feature scales, leading to suboptimal performance. Our proposed method establishes a multi-scale feature semantic network and employs a sophisticated fusion strategy to effectively integrate these features, resulting in improved semantic comprehension and inference. The core mechanism focuses on identifying and prioritizing key features across different scales, creating a richer and more robust representation of the underlying semantic relationships. This research addresses the limitations of existing methods by offering a more comprehensive and adaptable approach to semantic network analysis.

title: Dynamic Topological Space Transformations for Optimization
abstract: The optimization of complex systems often requires careful manipulation of their structure. Traditional optimization methods frequently rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting the system's adaptability. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topological space transformation optimization algorithm designed to automatically adjust transformation parameters, thereby enhancing system performance. We present a framework that leverages a dynamic mapping of the system's topological space, enabling the algorithm to optimize for specific performance metrics based on evolving system characteristics. The core mechanism involves a continuous, adaptive transformation process guided by a learned mapping, providing a flexible and robust solution for complex optimization problems. This approach overcomes the limitations of static optimization techniques by actively responding to changes in the system, leading to improved efficiency and robustness. This work explores the potential of dynamically mapping topological spaces to optimize system performance across diverse applications.

title: Nonlinear Topological Structures in Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning based on the principles of non-linear topological structures. The core concept is to dynamically adjust model parameters to enhance generalization performance through the inherent structural changes induced by this approach. We propose a method that leverages the flexibility of topological spaces to optimize model parameters in a way that is fundamentally different from traditional approaches. The system automatically adapts to the data, allowing for a more robust and adaptable model. This work addresses a critical challenge in machine learning by introducing a new approach that promotes better generalization.

title: Topological Protection of Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) utilizing topological protection. The core idea centers on leveraging the unique properties of anyons within topological insulators to physically protect quantum codes, thereby dramatically enhancing their resilience against noise. Traditional QEC schemes often rely on classical communication channels for redundancy, introducing latency and complexity. In contrast, our proposed method constructs a physical layer redundancy through the entanglement of anyons within a topological material. This approach offers a more robust and intrinsically fault-tolerant system. We present a theoretical framework outlining the implementation of specific QEC codes—specifically the Shor code—protected by topological anyon entanglement. The resulting system demonstrates a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to conventional approaches. The key innovations include the mapping of quantum information onto anyon states and the utilization of braiding operations to maintain the encoded information's integrity. Further investigation explores the scalability and practical considerations associated with this topological protection strategy.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-based modeling techniques for complex systems, with a particular focus on leveraging quantum potentials as a fundamental model. We explore how utilizing quantum machine learning algorithms to optimize system parameters can significantly enhance prediction accuracy and efficiency. The core claim is that by shifting the focus of complex system modeling towards quantum potentials, a novel approach to prediction can be achieved, offering a significant advancement over existing classical methods. The paper details the methodology, results, and potential implications of this approach, highlighting the advantages of quantum-enhanced modeling in predicting complex phenomena.

title: Bayesian Inference Engine Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to probabilistic inference by emulating the mechanisms of biological neural networks. Traditional probabilistic inference engines often rely on classical logic or graph models, lacking a biologically inspired simulation of neural networks and their inherent probabilistic reasoning processes. This work introduces a Bayesian inference engine constructed upon a layered, distributed, and synapse-plasticity-based architecture, mirroring key features of biological neurons. The core mechanism involves probabilistic connections and information transmission between neurons, facilitating continuous updating of probabilistic beliefs and enabling complex inferences. The engine leverages concepts such as Bayesian updating, Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, and belief propagation, implemented within a network structure designed to mimic biological neural dynamics. The resulting system offers a potentially more robust and adaptive approach to probabilistic reasoning, particularly in scenarios where uncertainty is inherent and traditional methods struggle. This research lays the groundwork for a new paradigm in artificial intelligence, moving beyond purely symbolic approaches towards more biologically plausible models of cognition. ---

title: Temporal Relational Graph Embedding with Dynamic Context
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that addresses the limitations of existing methods in capturing the dynamic nature of evolving graphs. Traditional graph embedding techniques often rely on static representations, failing to account for the temporal changes in relationships between nodes. Our proposed method, Temporal Relational Graph Embedding with Dynamic Context (TRGDC), leverages a recurrent neural network to model the dynamic context of a graph, incorporating both relational information and the elapsed time since the last update. The core idea is to continuously adapt node embeddings based on these temporal and relational factors. We demonstrate that TRGDC significantly improves the representation of dynamic graphs compared to static embedding methods, achieving superior performance in downstream graph-related tasks. The key contributions of this work are the integration of temporal modeling with relational graph embedding and the utilization of a recurrent neural network for dynamic context representation.

title: Probability Logic Matrix Entropy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to entropy calculation based on probability logic matrices, designed to rigorously assess the robustness and stability of algorithms, particularly within the context of machine learning. Traditional entropy measures often focus on static performance, while this method integrates dynamic adjustments driven by machine learning to provide a more comprehensive evaluation. The core mechanism involves leveraging the inherent probabilistic nature of probability logic matrices to quantify the uncertainty and sensitivity of an algorithm to its input. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a focused study of a reinforcement learning algorithm, showcasing its ability to identify vulnerabilities and guide model refinement. The research explores how this method can contribute to enhanced model reliability and performance.

title: 基于量子态叠加的并行算法设计方法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to parallel algorithm design leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. The core concept involves decomposing a given problem into a superposition of quantum states, enabling parallel computation across these states. This methodology aims to achieve exponential speedups compared to traditional classical algorithms. The design methodology focuses on identifying suitable problems amenable to this superposition-based parallelization. The theoretical framework outlines the key steps in constructing such algorithms, emphasizing the importance of state preparation, quantum gate operations, and state measurement. We explore the potential impact of this technique on various computational domains, highlighting the challenges and opportunities associated with realizing quantum speedups. The presented approach offers a fundamentally new paradigm for algorithm design, potentially revolutionizing computational efficiency.

title: Quantum Probability Computation: An Adaptive Optimization Framework
abstract: Quantum probability computation (QPC) holds immense promise for advanced scientific discovery and technological innovation. However, the inherent complexity of QPC algorithms necessitates sophisticated optimization techniques to achieve efficient computation. This paper introduces an adaptive optimization framework for QPC, designed to automatically adjust parameters and minimize computational cost. The core mechanism involves dynamically modifying key parameters based on the problem's characteristics, leading to enhanced efficiency. We present a comprehensive overview of the framework's design, detailing the optimization strategy and its potential impact on QPC performance. This work addresses a critical limitation of traditional QPC approaches, offering a novel solution for improved scalability and throughput.

title: Quantum Error Correction for Classical Computing via Topological Encoding
abstract: This paper investigates a fundamentally new approach to quantum error correction (QEC) by employing topological encoding within classical materials. Traditional QEC relies on quantum mechanics and entanglement, presenting significant technological hurdles for implementation on conventional computers. Our proposed method leverages the inherent robustness of topological states, specifically the braiding of quasiparticles, to achieve error detection and correction without direct measurement of the encoded quantum states. The core idea involves mapping logical qubits to physical qubits based on the topological properties of the material. By carefully controlling and manipulating these quasiparticles, we can implement a fault-tolerant QEC scheme directly on classical hardware. This approach avoids the decoherence issues associated with quantum systems and offers a potentially scalable solution for QEC using readily available materials. We present a theoretical framework for this encoding scheme, outlining the key mathematical concepts and relationships involved. The proposed methodology represents a shift in perspective, moving from quantum to topological approaches for QEC, opening new avenues for computation and information processing.

evidence.abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, termed "Adaptive Quantum Topology" (AQT), designed to optimize quantum computation. The core principle of AQT leverages the unique properties of quantum topology – a mathematical concept describing the interconnectedness of quantum states – to enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. The paper details the framework's design, emphasizing its capacity to generate novel quantum circuits and improve overall computational performance. The significance of this work lies in its potential to overcome limitations of traditional approaches, offering a fundamentally different paradigm for quantum algorithm design. This research explores the mathematical foundations of AQT, outlining the key steps involved in generating and optimizing quantum circuits that exhibit enhanced coherence and fidelity. We present a rigorous analysis of the framework's performance with specific examples demonstrating its efficacy in various quantum computation tasks. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING STRATEGIES OF TRANSNATIONAL COMPANIES IN INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
abstract: The article examines the impact of artificial intelligence technologies on the transformation of marketing strategies of transnational companies in international business. The relevance of the study stems from the rapid expansion of the global artificial intelligence market and the fact that marketing and sales have consistently remained among the business functions with the highest intensity of AI adoption worldwide. For transnational companies, which coordinate marketing activities across dozens of national markets with different languages, consumer cultures and regulatory regimes, artificial intelligence directly affects the classical dilemma of international marketing between standardisation and adaptation: the technology promises to deliver globally consistent brand communication that is simultaneously tailored to local audiences at a scale and speed unattainable for traditional marketing organisations. The article discusses the main directions in which artificial intelligence penetrates the international marketing activity of transnational companies, including hyper-personalisation of customer experience based on machine learning, generative production of advertising and communication content, restructuring of organisational models of marketing departments, and localisation of global campaigns for national markets. Particular attention is paid to the experience of leading transnational corporations in the consumer goods, digital services and e-commerce sectors, as well as to the organisational conditions under which investments in artificial intelligence translate into measurable economic outcomes. The study also addresses the risks accompanying the diffusion of the technology, including changes in consumer attitudes towards AI-generated advertising, reputational threats, and the new regulatory environment created by the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act for companies operating in the European market. The consequences of the uneven global distribution of AI infrastructure, investment and competencies for the competitive positions of companies from developed and developing economies in international markets are considered as a separate dimension of the problem within the field of international economic relations.

title: Learnable composition for neural operators
abstract: Neural operators are fast, differentiable surrogates for physical simulation, but their accuracy often degrades when domain geometry, size, or operating conditions differ from training. Supervised adaptation can recover accuracy, but even a small target set requires costly high-fidelity simulations. We therefore ask how pretraining and transfer can be designed together to reduce this deployment cost. LatentDDM first pretrains a neural operator to predict fields on small subdomains. For a new setting, it freezes this operator and trains only a lightweight module that composes the local predictions. We evaluate our method on two complementary problems: steady Darcy flow, where long-range pressure coupling must extend across increasingly large porous domains, and unsteady incompressible flow around a pitching airfoil, where rollout errors compound as target pitching frequencies exceed the training range. Compared with the capacity-matched models that process the full domain at once, LatentDDM's error is 36-56% lower on larger Darcy domains after adaptation with 16 target simulations. It also improves 20-step field rollouts in fast-pitching airfoil flow, both zero-shot and after few-shot calibration. These results identify the co-designed local pretraining and composition-level transfer as a promising design principle for physical foundation models.

title: SurfSpec: Enhancing Off-Target-Agnostic Specificity by Bounding Pocket-Ligand Geometric Mismatch
abstract: Lead optimization in structure-based drug design aims to improve target binding while avoiding unintended interactions with off-target pockets. However, existing affinity-driven methods do not explicitly control specificity, whereas current specificity-aware approaches commonly require prior knowledge of off-target structures. We address off-target-agnostic specificity-aware lead optimization by analyzing the geometric mismatch between a ligand and the target pocket. We provide a conservative specificity lower bound for geometrically separated off-targets without requiring access to off-target structures. By metricizing pocket--ligand mismatch, the triangle inequality shows that reducing target--ligand mismatch improves a conservative lower bound on mismatch to a separated off-target class, which can be translated into a specificity lower bound through an empirical geometry--affinity calibration. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce SurfSpec, an off-target-agnostic lead optimization framework that iteratively grows ligands toward under-occupied regions of the target pocket surface. SurfSpec alternates between linker generation toward selected target-surface patches, which provides geometric pseudo-labels, and refinement under a pocket-conditioned ligand prior, which restores these pseudo-labels into valid ligands. On the CrossDocked2020 test set, SurfSpec reduces geometric mismatch and outperforms evaluated off-target-agnostic lead optimization baselines in empirical specificity, while maintaining competitive target-affinity improvement.

title: Effective Hamiltonian for an off-resonantly driven qubit-cavity system
abstract: Accurate modeling of driven light-matter interactions is essential for quantum technologies, where natural and synthetic atoms are used to store and process quantum information, mediate interactions between bosonic modes, and enable nonlinear operations. In systems subject to multitone drives, however, the theoretical description becomes challenging and existing models cannot quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. Here, we derive an effective Hamiltonian that retains slowly rotating terms, providing a general framework for accurately describing driven dynamics across platforms. As a concrete application, we validate the theory in circuit QED, where it quantitatively reproduces experimentally measured ac Stark shifts and captures key interactions such as two-mode squeezing and beam splitting. Our results establish a broadly applicable tool to engineer driven interactions in quantum information processing platforms.

title: Hidden States as Bounded Objects?
abstract: This is an application preprint in the Atacton Working Paper Series (ATACTON-WP-HMM-001, Version 1.0). It is not peer reviewed. It is an application freeze on representation architecture, not a fitted-model preprint. No EM results, no reader results, and no forecast results are claimed. The proposition is computational unity ≠ semantic unity: one latent path can be well-defined as a statistical co-representation of unlike series and still fail as one bounded historical object. Strategy A is a mixed-state representation; Strategy B is an object-separated representation. The paper also freezes the hierarchy observed variable ≠ semantic object ≠ latent state (X ≠ R ≠ Z): data-source multiplicity does not imply object multiplicity. Frozen Kₖ v1.0 (Wong, 2026c) is called, not rewritten. The same unplayed Premier League fixture as Application 1 (Ipswich Town v Liverpool, 4 September 2026) is bound on a different evidence layer: league result path plus dated pre-kick-off quotes, not the H2H page. The framework constrains the semantic interpretation of model components; it does not determine the statistically optimal factorisation. Correspondence: joe@atacton.com

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Explaining Next-Activity Prediction with Activity-Level Shapley Attributions
abstract: This software implements the framework presented in "Explaining Next-Activity Prediction with Activity-Level Shapley Attributions." It trains Transformer classifiers (BERT-base and RoBERTa-base) to predict the next activity of an ongoing case from its observed activity prefix and explains the predictions with SHAP at the level of complete activity occurrences. The package includes code for model training and evaluation, the ablation (Full, Scratch, and Frozen) and backbone experiments, SHAP explanations, the comparison with LIME in faithfulness and runtime, and the aggregation of results and statistical tests across random seeds. The benchmark event logs and trained models are not redistributed; the README lists the public sources of the datasets and the steps to reproduce all results. Version 1.1.0 revises the README to follow the journal's reproducibility guidelines, adds an MIT License, and sets the default training batch size to 32, as reported in the manuscript.

title: Dual Optimisation in Low-Resource Natural Language Processing: Integrating Meta-Learning and Efficient Deep Architectures for Sustainable AI Development
abstract: This study addresses a critical gap in low-resource Natural Language Processing (NLP): the lack of aunified framework that jointly optimises computational efficiency and task performance under severe dataand hardware constraints. To bridge this gap, the study introduces the Dual Optimisation Framework—thefirst empirically validated approach integrating meta-learning (MAML) with resource-adaptivearchitectures (DistilBERT and MobileBERT). A mixed-methods design was used: quantitative experimentsmeasured accuracy, F1-scores, latency, and memory consumption across multiple configurations, whilequalitative expert interviews contextualised deployment feasibility in low-resource settings. Results showthat DistilBERT combined with MAML improves efficiency–performance trade-offs by up to 35%,outperforming larger models while maintaining competitive accuracy. Latency and memory profilingconfirm the framework’s suitability for computational realities in the Global South. The study contributes ascalable, sustainable model for equitable NLP development and demonstrates how learning efficiency andcomputational efficiency can be co-optimised in constrained environments.

title: Dynamic Quantum Information Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum information encoding technique designed to adapt to environmental changes and target behaviors, resulting in more intelligent signal processing and data transmission. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust encoding strategies. Traditional encoding methods are static and require pre-defined parameters, offering limited adaptability. This work proposes a fundamentally new approach that allows for real-time, self-optimizing encoding, potentially revolutionizing data communication and signal processing. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.
