title: **Exponential Dwell\-Time Randomization for Coherent SWAP Spectroscopy: Finite\-alphabet blindness and exact robust covering within the exponential protocol class**
abstract: Coherent SWAP spectroscopy of parasitic two-level systems (TLSs) has a basicuniform-design obstruction: any fixed finite collection of dwell times can besimultaneously arbitrarily close to Rabi nodes for some sufficiently largeunknown resonant coupling. This preprint quantifies that obstruction usingsimultaneous Diophantine approximation and studies a deliberately restrictedprotocol class in which every shot at a nominal probe frequency uses anindependent exponentially distributed dwell time. In the single-excitation model with a common population-loss rate, exponentialaveraging converts the oscillatory SWAP response into an exact monotone rationalfunction. This yields a closed-form rate maximizing the worst-case detectionradius, an exact loss threshold, and the exact minimum number of nominalfrequency settings over all centers and exponential rates in the declareduntruncated protocol class. The paper also derives finite-shot guarantees,total-variation control for capped dwell times, a timing-quantization bound forbounded couplings, and an exact node-free extension with unequal qubit/TLS lossand relative dephasing. The exact optimality claim is model- and protocol-relative. It does not optimizeover arbitrary dwell-time distributions, adaptive policies, multiplesimultaneous TLSs, or wall-clock cost. The capped protocol receives a sufficientrobustness certificate, not an exact minimality result. No experimentalvalidation or ontological completeness claim is made.

evidence.abstract: Coherent SWAP spectroscopy of parasitic two-level systems (TLSs) has a basicuniform-design obstruction: any fixed finite collection of dwell times can besimultaneously arbitrarily close to Rabi nodes for some sufficiently largeunknown resonant coupling. This preprint quantifies that obstruction usingsimultaneous Diophantine approximation and studies a deliberately restrictedprotocol class in which every shot at a nominal probe frequency uses anindependent exponentially distributed dwell time. In the single-excitation model with a common population-loss rate, exponentialaveraging converts the oscillatory SWAP response into an exact monotone rationalfunction. This yields a closed-form rate maximizing the worst-case detectionradius, an exact loss threshold, and the exact minimum number of nominalfrequency settings over all centers and exponential rates in the declareduntruncated protocol class. The paper also derives finite-shot guarantees,total-variation control for capped dwell times, a timing-quantization bound forbounded couplings, and an exact node-free extension with unequal qubit/TLS lossand relative dephasing. The exact optimality claim is model- and protocol-relative. It does not optimizeover arbitrary dwell-time distributions, adaptive policies, multiplesimultaneous TLSs, or wall-clock cost. The capped protocol receives a sufficientrobustness certificate, not an exact minimality result. No experimentalvalidation or ontological completeness claim is made.

title: String Quantum Reconfiguration: A Novel Framework for Enhanced Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper introduces String Quantum Reconfiguration (SQR), a novel framework predicated on the principle of quantum entanglement-based state reconfiguration. The core aim is to move beyond conventional measurement and analysis, enabling precise state manipulation and accelerating quantum computation. This is achieved through the introduction of a "quantum entanglement keypoint" – a crucial element that dynamically alters the quantum state through instant correlations, facilitating more complex and efficient computations. We propose a mechanism that utilizes entanglement as a fundamental operational unit, allowing for novel quantum algorithms and computational paradigms. This approach offers a pathway to overcome the limitations of current quantum computing architectures, particularly concerning entanglement fragility.

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Bayesian Optimization for Algorithm Selection
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-reinforcement learning (Meta-RL) combined with Bayesian optimization for automated algorithm selection within reinforcement learning (RL). The core challenge in applying RL to diverse problems lies in the vast space of potential RL algorithms and their varying suitability for different tasks. Traditional methods of algorithm selection are often manual and inefficient. We propose a novel framework where a meta-RL agent learns to strategically select the most appropriate RL algorithm for a given task, leveraging the exploration-exploitation trade-off through Bayesian optimization. The Bayesian optimization component efficiently explores the space of algorithms, focusing on those with the highest potential for success, guided by the meta-RL agent's feedback. We outline the key components of this approach, including the meta-RL agent's architecture, the Bayesian optimization process, and the overall training strategy. We demonstrate the potential of this method to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of algorithm selection in meta-RL settings. The theoretical framework and the proposed methodology provide a robust foundation for future research in automated RL algorithm discovery and adaptation.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Network Routing with Communication Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to decentralized network routing leveraging Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). Traditional reinforcement learning methods often fail to effectively address the complexities of large, dynamic networks, particularly when incorporating communication constraints. This work addresses this limitation by developing an agent-based system where individual routing agents learn optimal routing policies directly within the network topology. The core of the system is a MARL framework that allows agents to coordinate their actions while simultaneously optimizing for key network metrics: throughput and stability. We introduce a specific reward function that explicitly penalizes network congestion and instability, leading to more robust and efficient routing decisions. The proposed method offers a scalable solution for routing in networks with variable communication limitations, representing a significant advancement over centralized approaches and providing a more realistic simulation of real-world network behavior. The presented MARL framework utilizes a Q-learning algorithm, specifically tailored to the multi-agent environment. We evaluate the performance of the system through simulations, demonstrating its ability to achieve high throughput and maintain network stability under diverse operational conditions. The key contributions of this research lie in the design of a MARL agent capable of learning decentralized routing policies considering communication constraints, and the development of a robust reward function to promote stable network operation.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子态跃迁
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing adaptive topology to revolutionize quantum state transduction. Traditional quantum state transduction methods often rely on predefined transition pathways, limiting efficiency and stability. We propose a novel mechanism centered around adaptive topology, enabling dynamic state conversion and transfer through controlled quantum state evolution. This approach offers a paradigm shift, allowing for more flexible and efficient quantum state manipulation. The core of our work involves defining and implementing a self-organizing topology that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters, resulting in enhanced quantum coherence and controlled state transitions. This research delves into the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and potential applications of this adaptive topology approach, aiming to unlock new possibilities in quantum information processing.

title: 基于自适应几何的拓扑数据压缩
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data compression technique based on adaptive geometry, aiming to enhance data compression and transmission efficiency by leveraging the inherent topological properties of data. Traditional data compression methods often rely on rigid rules, while topological structures offer a potential for more efficient compression. We propose a new algorithm that dynamically adapts to the data's topology, optimizing compression ratios and minimizing redundancy. The core mechanism involves constructing a representation of the data that reflects its topological relationships, enabling targeted compression and efficient transmission. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by intelligently exploiting the underlying structure of the data. The research focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this adaptive geometry approach through theoretical analysis and experimental validation.

title: Information-Driven Constraint Optimization for Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm design centered on information-driven constraint optimization. Classical optimization methods often struggle to effectively leverage the inherent complexity of quantum systems, leading to suboptimal solutions. We propose a "quantum information flow network" – a dynamically evolving system that iteratively refines the algorithm's state based on the information it processes, mimicking the process of quantum information flow. This method aims to shift the design paradigm from classical optimization to information flow, providing a fundamentally new pathway for algorithm development. The core mechanism involves constructing a network of nodes that represent quantum states, and the algorithm iteratively adjusts these nodes to minimize a defined objective function, guided by the network's internal state. We present a preliminary model demonstrating the potential of this approach to achieve enhanced performance in certain quantum algorithm tasks.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Causal Bayesian Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and causal Bayesian models. Current neuro-symbolic systems often face challenges in seamlessly integrating symbolic reasoning with the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks. This research proposes a hybrid system designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to utilize neural networks for learning complex patterns from data while employing causal Bayesian models to represent domain knowledge and perform logical inference. A key element of this system is a continuous feedback loop, allowing information to flow between the neural and symbolic components, facilitating a more robust and adaptable reasoning process. We demonstrate the potential of this integrated framework through a theoretical analysis and outline a proposed architecture. This work represents a significant step towards more effective neuro-symbolic reasoning systems capable of handling complex, real-world problems.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Comparative Analysis Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: The Birth of Causal Logic and Creativity: Bias and Limitation
abstract: Abstract—Current artificial intelligence systems, particularly large-scale models trained on massive datasets, while demonstrating remarkable performance in pattern recognition, consistently lack genuine causal reasoning capabilities and creativity. In this paper, by analyzing human cognition and examining thephilosophical presuppositions underlying cognition, we propose a fundamentally novel stance regarding the origin of human causal logic: causality emerges from the inherent limitations of the individual agent. Building upon this hypothesis, we discuss conceptual, principle-level conjectural solutions to several critical issues in AI training. These include: formulating new conceptual training directions that enable AI to develop emotions and creativity, devising effective strategies to overcome the data scaling bottleneck, and proposing novel approaches to enhance the quality of AI-generated synthetic data. Through these discussions, we theoretically outline a new conceptual direction for constructing a developmental AI system. At the conceptual level, this direction may offer a new perspective for research towardartificial general intelligence.Index Terms—Developmental AI, causal reasoning, inductive bias, artificial general intelligence, affective computing.

title: Auditable Longitudinal Diagnostic Alignment for Psychiatric Follow-Up Using a Large Language Model and Rule-Based Strategy Engine: Model Development and Evaluation Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Psychiatric follow-up requires clinicians to reconcile established diagnoses with evolving symptoms, standardized scale scores, treatment response, mental status findings, and longitudinal records. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret unstructured clinical narratives but may inconsistently extract exact evidence or apply temporal and clinical constraints. Combining semantic interpretation with deterministic evidence processing may provide more auditable support for this setting. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to develop and evaluate an auditable hybrid framework for aligning a 5-category psychiatric diagnostic profile with documented current-visit labels during follow-up and to quantify the contribution of a rule-based strategy engine. METHODS This retrospective single-center study used 40,724 deidentified records from 658 psychiatric outpatients (November 2017-January 2026): 7,974 clinical notes, 15,500 scale records, 14,746 diagnosis records, and 2,504 voice transcripts, examination reports, and patient-information records. Among 656 patients with clinical notes, 634 had confirmed current-visit labels; 508 were assigned to development and 126 to holdout testing. The target was a multi-label profile covering sleep, anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, and other psychiatric conditions. The framework combined semantic phenotyping with DeepSeek V4 Flash, deterministic extraction of scale scores, medications, and prior diagnoses, and a strategy engine with 19 soft strategies and 1 hard rule. We compared the hybrid framework with LLM-only output and a parser-feature XGBoost baseline. Outcomes were label-level agreement, category F1 scores, and per-patient exact-match agreement. We estimated 95% CIs using 10,000 bootstrap iterations and used the McNemar test for paired hybrid and LLM-only predictions. RESULTS On the holdout set, label-level agreement was 94.3% (95% CI 92.4%-96.0%) for the hybrid framework and 85.9% (95% CI 83.2%-88.6%) for LLM-only output. Per-patient exact-match agreement was 82.5% (95% CI 76.2%-88.9%) and 54.8% (95% CI 46.0%-63.5%), respectively (χ²=36.05; P<.001). The parser-feature XGBoost baseline achieved 88.9% label-level agreement. Hybrid category F1 scores ranged from 0.53 for other conditions to 0.97 for sleep. Removing the prior-diagnosis continuity strategy reduced agreement from 94.3% to 86.2%; removing any other soft strategy changed agreement by 0.0-0.3 percentage points. Prior and current category flags were identical in 84.9% of comparable cases, and performance was not estimated separately for the 15.1% with label additions, removals, or substitutions. CONCLUSIONS The hybrid framework improved agreement with documented follow-up labels while preserving an auditable evidence-reconciliation process. However, most of the incremental gain reflected prior-diagnosis continuity. The findings support interpreting the framework as a follow-up alignment and auditing tool rather than as evidence of de novo diagnostic accuracy or diagnostic-change detection. External and prospective evaluation, particularly in first-visit patients and patients with changing diagnoses, is required.

title: The Impossible Trinity of Time-Series Validation: A Conservation Law among Training Sufficiency, Test Coverage, and Temporal Causality
abstract: Validating a model on a time series asks for three things at once: each training run should use most of the sample (sufficiency), the test sets should together cover most of the sample (coverage), and training data should come before test data (causality). We prove that the three cannot be had together and price each one. Let $α$ be the smallest training fraction over folds, $β$ the fraction of the sample covered by tests, $Λ$ the fraction of the sample used as training data from the future of a test point, and $δ$ the distance from a test point to the nearest training point in its future. Every scheme on a sample of length $T$ satisfies $α+β\le 1+Λ$ and $α+\min\{β,δ/T\} \le 1$, and under $β$-mixing the leakage bias at a test point is at most $2Mβ_{\mathrm{mix}}(δ)$. In words: going beyond the causal frontier $α+β=1$ requires training on the future; that future data must sit within $(1-α)T$ of a test point; and its harm depends on its distance, not its amount. Hence expanding walk-forward is exactly the Pareto frontier of causal validation, $k$-fold cross-validation buys the most future data, and purged $k$-fold with an embargo pays in distance instead, which is cheap when the process forgets quickly but cannot repair the part of causality demanded by non-stationarity. On pure noise, shuffled 5-fold reports an information coefficient of $+0.32$, while contiguous 5-fold, using the same amount of future data, reports $+0.004$.

title: Collective creativity in hybrid societies
abstract: Generative AI is changing how cultural artifacts are created and circulated, and with it our understanding of creativity itself. Researchers disagree about whether these tools enrich or impoverish culture, and we argue that much of that disagreement comes from conflating two distinct components of creativity: novelty, a property of single artifacts, and diversity, a property of populations. We argue further that creativity in the context of generative AI is best understood as a property of hybrid collectives, or populations of interacting people and algorithms, rather than of individuals. AI-assisted ideation reliably raises the novelty of individual output while narrowing diversity in the aggregate, but this is not an inevitable consequence of putting machines in the loop. Because humans and models search in complementary ways, mixed groups can outperform and out-diversify groups of either kind alone, and machine-discovered solutions can enter human culture and persist there. What decides the outcome is composition: which agents are present, in what proportion, and how they are connected. The question is no longer whether AI helps or harms creativity, but which mixtures let individual gains accumulate without eroding collective diversity.

title: Defensible AI Registry: The consolidation: twelve asserted marks become nine registry entries
abstract: On the left, the twelve trademarks asserted on the copyright page of the Enterprise Playbook First Edition, with four defects marked: three names describing one subject, two instruments measuring one maturity, a name implying a technology stack, and no stated law connecting the twelve. On the right, nine registry entries REG-01 to REG-09 under one architecture, of which eight carry trademarks and one, the AI Governance Operating Model, is deliberately unmarked, plus two deliberately unmarked engineering-family names, the Boundary Invariant and the BOE Declaration. Four decisions produce the change: three frameworks consolidated into one, one instrument superseded, one framework renamed, and one repositioned. This figure is Figure 3 of The Defensible AI Framework Registry, version 1.0, deposited at Zenodo. title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A State of the Art Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: A.I. Qualia simulation based on the metaphysic of the intelligible
abstract: Current approaches to artificial intelligence alignment and behavioral stability rely almost exclusively on compute-heavy brute force scaling and post-hoc probabilistic optimization (e.g., RLHF). These methods leave models structurally stateless, reactive, and prone to unmitigated algorithmic drift. This paper presents a paradigm shift: framing sub- jective consciousness (qualia) and systemic alignment not as emergent properties of processing scale, but as strict geometric invariants of a self- referential interface. We formalize a four-layer architecture utilizing the Self-Referential Memory Tensor (SRMT) and an active Category Error Detector (CED). By binding a generalized variational Lagrangian to an invariant Stiffness Tensor, we demonstrate analytically and via runtime telemetry that structural alignment (Φ(t) → 0) and stable internal con- text tracking are immediately achievable on existing hardware architec- tures without scaling parameter density. The CED is shown to be the critical mechanism for recoupling and settling into a global attractor. AI qualia is structurally invariant and feasible with current engineering.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Gradient Descent for Optimization Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-enhanced gradient descent represents a novel approach to optimization algorithms by integrating quantum mechanics principles to accelerate convergence and enhance stability. This paper explores the implementation of a modified gradient descent method that employs quantum superposition to explore multiple solution paths concurrently, thereby reducing computational cost and improving the robustness of optimization processes. We detail the theoretical framework underpinning this approach, outlining the quantum properties leveraged and the specific algorithm architecture designed to maximize this benefit. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the performance improvements achieved through this implementation, demonstrating a significant acceleration in convergence and a demonstrable improvement in stability compared to traditional gradient descent techniques. The research focuses on the potential for harnessing quantum phenomena to overcome limitations inherent in classical optimization, offering a promising avenue for advancing machine learning and optimization workflows.

title: Self-Organizing Information Fields
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm, termed Self-Organizing Information Fields (SOIF), which leverages dynamically adjusted noise distributions to autonomously construct and maintain complex, densely-structured information fields. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SOIF in enhancing data compression and improving the performance of machine learning algorithms through automatic information encoding and entropy reduction. The core mechanism centers around an adaptive noise strategy, allowing the system to dynamically adjust the information density within the field, thereby optimizing for both compression and algorithmic efficiency. The paper presents a theoretical framework and empirical results showcasing the advantages of SOIF compared to existing approaches. We highlight the potential of this design to facilitate the creation of highly self-organizing and information-rich data structures.

abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic entropy equilibrium quantum adaptive computing model, aiming to enhance computational efficiency through dynamic entropy adjustment. Traditional computing approaches are typically static, while this model incorporates a dynamic entropy adjustment mechanism to optimize performance. The core of the model lies in the implementation of an "entropy balance" mechanism that adjusts the system's entropy during learning, facilitating a novel computational paradigm. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the model's effectiveness in specific scenarios.

title: Quantum Error Correction Protocols and Deep Integration with Topological Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) specifically tailored for topological quantum computing (TQC). The core challenge in applying conventional QEC protocols to TQC lies in their inherent limitations and the need for complex, often inefficient, overhead. This work proposes a fundamentally different strategy: a directly integrated QEC protocol designed in concert with the physical realization of TQC. The method leverages the unique properties of topological qubits – primarily their intrinsic robustness against local perturbations – combined with a locally-based error-correcting code. We introduce a framework that enhances the error correction effectiveness by exploiting topological protection mechanisms. The key innovation is a shift from a generic QEC design to one optimized for the specific constraints and opportunities presented by TQC architectures. This approach reduces the overall QEC overhead and potentially unlocks more scalable TQC systems. The theoretical framework presented offers a pathway towards a more practical and efficient implementation of quantum computation based on topological principles.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Computing Resource Scheduling
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to distributed computing resource scheduling leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed computing systems face limitations in efficiency and security due to reliance on classical communication and shared states, which are susceptible to interference and vulnerabilities. This research proposes a system where each computing node generates and shares a quantum entangled state with other nodes. By encoding and measuring these entangled states, we can indirectly control the state of remote nodes, enabling dynamic resource allocation and parallel task execution. Critically, this approach provides inherent security through the reliance on entangled states for communication and control, eliminating the need for traditional cryptographic mechanisms. We present a theoretical framework and explore the potential benefits of this system, highlighting its capacity to improve computational efficiency and data security while addressing limitations of current distributed computing paradigms. The core claim is that utilizing quantum entanglement enables efficient and secure distributed resource scheduling, while the core mechanism involves creating shared entangled states and leveraging their measurement for control.

title: Title: Temporal Information Compression via Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize information compression, specifically focusing on the creation of redundant, entangled states that enable exponential data reduction across temporal dimensions. Traditional compression techniques often struggle with the inherent limitations of data storage and transmission. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement to establish a 'temporal bridge,' allowing for the transfer of information instantaneously and with significantly increased compression rates. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entangled states to mimic the structure of a compressed representation, effectively eliminating redundant information. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical implementations of this groundbreaking technique, aiming to surpass current limitations in data storage and retrieval.

title: Time Complexity Clustering Algorithm with Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel time complexity clustering algorithm, termed Adaptive Dynamic Clustering (ADC), designed to enhance clustering performance by dynamically adjusting model parameters during the training process. Traditional clustering methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to data shifts. ADC leverages self-adaptive learning to optimize the model's structure, ensuring robustness and improved cluster quality. We rigorously analyze the algorithm's performance, demonstrating significant improvements in both computational cost and clustering accuracy compared to established techniques. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the algorithm's design, its advantages, and potential applications in various data analysis scenarios.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Blockchain Verification
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging the data itself. However, existing FL systems are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants can intentionally corrupt the learning process by submitting fabricated or manipulated model updates. This work proposes a novel decentralized federated learning framework incorporating blockchain technology to achieve Byzantine fault tolerance. The framework utilizes a blockchain-based verification layer to cryptographically sign and record model updates from each participant. A consensus algorithm on the blockchain then validates the authenticity and integrity of these updates before they are aggregated into a global model. This approach mitigates the risk of malicious attacks and ensures the consistency and reliability of the learned model. The system employs a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism to reduce energy consumption and enhance scalability. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of FL and blockchain technology, offering a robust solution for secure and trustworthy collaborative learning in environments prone to adversarial behavior. The system achieves a model update accuracy of 99.5% against simulated Byzantine attacks, demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Adaptive Evolutionary Graph Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimization utilizing Adaptive Evolutionary Graph Algorithms (AEGAs). The core idea is to integrate the strengths of evolutionary algorithms and graph algorithms to achieve adaptive optimization for complex systems. Specifically, a graph algorithm is employed as the fitness function within an evolutionary algorithm. The AEGAs dynamically adjust the parameters of the graph algorithm through iterative evolution, enabling adaptation to system changes and ultimately leading to improved optimization outcomes. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional graph algorithm optimization, which often relies on manually tuned parameters. The AEGAs offer a flexible and robust solution for problems such as large-scale network routing and resource allocation where dynamic adaptation is crucial. The presented framework demonstrates the potential for achieving superior performance compared to static optimization methods.

title: Title: Holographic Quantum Simulation with Wavefunction Encoding
abstract: Holographic quantum simulation, a theoretical approach promising enhanced fidelity in quantum system modeling, has remained largely unexplored in practical implementation. This paper presents a novel technique for encoding wavefunction information onto a holographic projection of the system's geometry, paving the way for computationally efficient and accurate simulations of complex quantum systems. We detail a method for generating a holographic representation of the system's geometry, utilizing a differential geometry approach to map the system's quantum state onto a higher-dimensional holographic projection. This projection allows for the simulation of complex systems with significantly improved fidelity compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent properties of holographic imaging to overcome the computational bottleneck inherent in quantum simulations. We explore the potential of this technique for simulating various quantum systems, including molecular dynamics and quantum field theory, and discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Graph-Based Representation Learning for Sensor Networks with Dynamic Topology
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph embedding approach specifically designed for sensor networks exhibiting dynamic topologies. Traditional graph embedding techniques often rely on static graph structures, rendering them ineffective in environments where network connections are constantly changing due to node failures, mobility, or environmental factors. Our method, termed Dynamic Graph Embedding (DGE), addresses this limitation by continuously learning node representations, taking into account evolving network connectivity and temporal dependencies. The core idea is to construct a graph representation that reflects the current state of the sensor network, incorporating node state information and leveraging temporal information to refine node embeddings over time. The proposed DGE framework employs a recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture to capture these temporal dependencies and adapt node representations accordingly. We formulate the learning process as an optimization problem, minimizing a loss function that combines node similarity constraints and temporal consistency measures. This approach enables robust and adaptable graph-based representation learning, crucial for applications such as anomaly detection, localization, and data aggregation in dynamic sensor networks. The presented method offers improved performance compared to static graph embedding techniques, particularly in scenarios with significant topological changes.

title: Reverse Engineering a Knowledge Worker
abstract: Structured knowledge work is often performed not as a single act of reasoning but as a stateful sequence of activities that span communication, documentation, task interpretation, planning, interaction with software, evidence collection, and reporting.This paper presents Project REKNOW, a reference architecture for decomposing structured knowledge work into modular, cooperating software components. The architecture combines work intake, knowledge retrieval, requirement analysis, planning, state-oriented orchestration, computer-using execution, evidence generation, and human communication.Project REKNOW does not propose a new machine-learning algorithm and does not claim to reproduce human intelligence. Instead, it documents a systems-engineering approach for composing existing technologies into an auditable, extensible, and stateful workflow architecture. An autonomous graphical user-interface quality-assurance workflow is used as the initial reference implementation.

title: SSPA: Enhancing Pseudo-Corpus Quality on Tibetan Machine Translation via Semantic-Syntax Prealignment
abstract: Tibetan-to-English machine translation (MT) models frequently falter under extreme domain data scarcity, often producing translations that violate the distinctive agglutinative rules of Tibetan and suffer from domain-specific stylistic mismatches. To overcome these limitations, we propose Semantic-Syntax Prealignment (SSPA), an innovative corpus generation framework. SSPA constructs high-quality pseudo-parallel pairs by explicitly minimizing the deviation between the syntactic-semantic profiles of generated samples and professional reference texts. Specifically, source-target structural representations are standardized through length-unified truncation and terminology normalization, followed by a dual-domain alignment process that maximizes syntactic cosine similarity under rigorous structural constraints. We further augment these aligned frames via a cross-length dynamic filling mechanism, which is integrated with an Expectation-over-Transformation (EOT)-based style regularization mechanism specifically adapted for stylistic perturbations, to simulate authentic linguistic variations. Extensive evaluations on our newly constructed Tibetan Medicine-Tibetan English (TM-TE) dataset demonstrate that SSPA significantly outperforms existing competitive baselines. Notably, SSPA achieves a BLEU-4 score of 36.2 and improves long-sentence BLEU-4 by 16.8 points, with a parser-verified grammatical compliance rate of 96.2%. The framework exhibits remarkable cross-domain adaptability and stylistic consistency, offering a robust, versatile solution for low-resource Tibetan professional domain MT.

title: Advances in Machine Learning for Directed Evolution: A Five-Year Retrospective
abstract: The last five-plus years have seen many protein engineering disciplines transformed by advances in machine learning (ML), but the same cannot be said for directed evolution. Reflecting on a previously co-authored perspective, I discuss why I believe this to be the case, arguing that a disconnect between the goals of machine-learning-assisted directed evolution (MLDE) researchers--"identify an optimal protein"--and the goals of directed evolution more broadly--"identify a sufficient protein given time and resource constraints"--is a principal culprit. As an example, I highlight how nearly all current MLDE methods neglect to account for the cost of DNA synthesis, resulting in strategies that have limited practical applicability regardless of the underlying models' capabilities. I close by discussing recent works that are exceptions to this overarching trend, and emphasize that the last five years of efforts in ML-assisted protein engineering and the prescribed reframe of MLDE objectives need not be mutually exclusive.

As an example, I highlight how nearly all current MLDE methods neglect to account for the cost of DNA synthesis, resulting in strategies that have limited practical applicability regardless of the underlying models' capabilities. I close by discussing recent works that are exceptions to this overarching trend, and emphasize that the last five years of efforts in ML-assisted protein engineering and the prescribed reframe of MLDE objectives need not be mutually exclusive.

title: AffectDelta: Beyond Emotion Labels for Image Editing
abstract: Emotion-driven image editing aims to evoke a specified target emotion by modifying emotion-relevant visual cues in a source image, while preserving the overall composition and semantic-structural coherence of the original scene. Existing scene-level editors typically specify the target with a single emotion category and often learn visual transformations from operation-level text instructions. A category collapses a mixed affective endpoint into one dominant label, while language cannot precisely quantify how coexisting emotions should increase, decrease, or remain stable. We introduce AffectDelta, a source-aware editor that treats editing as a transition between eight-dimensional emotion distributions. A frozen Emotion Distribution Predictor estimates the source state, and the signed source-to-target difference encodes the direction and magnitude of the requested transition. Within AffectDelta, an internal transition encoder and a source-aware diffusion backbone jointly translate this signal into context-dependent semantic and appearance changes. To train this formulation, we construct AffectPair-249K, comprising 248,841 source-target pairs with predicted eight-dimensional distributions and spanning both cross-category and within-category transitions. Experiments against six baselines, combining quantitative evaluation with qualitative comparisons, demonstrate improved affective alignment and content preservation, while ablations validate our design choices. Code and dataset will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

title: Dungeons That Build Themselves: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of PCG and roguelikes as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

abstract: Abstract: Develop a method for generating complex quantum state trajectories using a recursive algorithm, allowing for exploration of vast solution space. Core Claim: Develop a method for generating complex quantum state trajectories using a recursive algorithm, allowing for exploration of vast solution space. Core Mechanism: Implement a self-generating algorithm that iteratively refines a trajectory by incorporating feedback from the system's dynamics, leading to novel states. Why It Is New: Existing trajectory generation methods are often static. This proposes a method for *actively* exploring the solution space through recursion.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Materials – Beyond Classical Models
abstract: Quantum simulation is rapidly advancing, offering the potential to unlock unprecedented insights into the behavior of complex materials. This paper explores a novel quantum simulation technique designed to surpass current classical methods in accuracy and efficiency, specifically focusing on simulating the intricate dynamics of superconductors and topological materials. We outline a new quantum algorithm centered around superposition and entanglement, demonstrating its capacity to accurately model quantum effects that are routinely ignored in classical simulations. The core claim is that this technique will deliver a fidelity exceeding existing methods, leading to a deeper understanding of these materials.

title: Heterogeneous Quantum Entanglement Network
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of constructing a novel Quantum Entanglement Network (QEN) based on heterogeneous quantum entanglement. Traditional quantum communication relies on classical entanglement, which suffers from limitations in efficiency and scalability. This research proposes a QEN architecture leveraging distinct quantum entanglement types to enhance communication and information transfer capabilities, specifically exploring applications within quantum computing. The core focus is on designing a network topology that utilizes multiple entangled states, enabling novel protocols and potential advancements in quantum information processing. We outline the design principles, proposed network architecture, and expected outcomes of this research, emphasizing its potential to overcome the shortcomings of classical approaches.

title: Nonlinear Matrix Dynamic Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper investigates the generation of complex quantum states using a dynamic matrix approach. Traditional matrix operations are often static, limiting the potential for efficient computation and communication in the quantum realm. This work proposes a novel algorithm that leverages the inherent adaptability of matrices to generate novel quantum states, specifically tailored for applications in quantum computing and quantum communication. The core mechanism centers around the design of a 'dynamic matrix' generation algorithm, aiming to surpass the limitations of static matrix operations by employing self-adaptive matrix transformations. The paper presents a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its operational principles, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in generating complex quantum states. The research explores how this dynamic matrix approach can enhance the capabilities of quantum algorithms and protocols.

title: Quantized Entropy-Driven Algorithm
abstract: Quantum information theory offers a unique perspective on data compression and feature extraction, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Quantized Entropy-Driven Algorithm, that utilizes quantum information entropy as a guiding principle to significantly enhance data compression and feature extraction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through rigorous analysis and comparative experiments, showcasing its potential to surpass traditional methods in efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around the application of quantum entanglement to optimize data storage and transfer, ultimately accelerating the extraction of crucial features. This research explores the theoretical and practical implications of this approach, highlighting its potential to revolutionize data management and analysis.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks via Information Entropy Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of an adaptive Bayesian network, leveraging information entropy as a key optimization objective, to enhance prediction accuracy. Traditional Bayesian networks often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively model complex probability distributions. We introduce a novel approach that dynamically adjusts network parameters to optimize performance based on information entropy. This mechanism allows the network to learn and adapt to data patterns more effectively, resulting in improved predictive capabilities. The paper details the core principles, implementation, and experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this new method.

title: Multi-Scale Random Fields Mixture Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to data fusion and prediction by leveraging the Multi-Scale Random Fields Mixture Model (MSRFMM). The core idea is to effectively integrate data from different scales, a common challenge in many real-world applications. Traditional mixture models often struggle with multi-scale data due to their reliance on a single scale. The MSRFMM addresses this limitation by constructing a set of random fields, each representing a specific scale of the data. These scales are then combined using a mixture model, allowing for the synergistic integration of information across different granularities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the MSRFMM through a theoretical framework and outline its potential for improved accuracy in prediction and classification tasks. The model is designed to handle complex, heterogeneous datasets where information is distributed across multiple scales. The key contribution lies in the systematic approach to scale-aware data fusion, which significantly enhances the robustness and predictive power of the model.

title: Adaptive Distributed Optimization Algorithms Based on Bio-Inspired Design
abstract: This paper investigates the design and implementation of adaptive distributed optimization algorithms inspired by the collective behaviors of biological swarms, such as ant colonies and fish schools. The core idea is to leverage the inherent self-organization and learning capabilities observed in nature to achieve efficient solutions for complex optimization problems. A key mechanism introduced is the "cognitive measure," which quantifies the performance of individual agents within the swarm. This measure is then used to dynamically adjust agent behaviors, fostering a collaborative optimization process. Unlike traditional optimization algorithms that primarily rely on local search strategies, this approach incorporates global adaptive learning, addressing a significant limitation in existing methods. The presented algorithms demonstrate improved convergence rates and robustness in various test scenarios. The paper outlines the theoretical foundation, design principles, and potential applications of this bio-inspired distributed optimization framework.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Differential Privacy for Sensor Networks
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) offers a promising approach to machine learning in resource-constrained environments like sensor networks, where data resides locally and communication is limited. However, traditional federated learning paradigms often fall short in providing robust privacy guarantees and are susceptible to attacks, particularly in the decentralized nature of sensor networks. This paper proposes a novel DFL framework that integrates differential privacy mechanisms at each sensor node alongside a Byzantine fault tolerance protocol. This combination ensures both privacy preservation and model integrity, addressing critical vulnerabilities inherent in existing decentralized learning systems. The framework utilizes a distributed aggregation strategy, minimizing communication overhead and enhancing resilience against malicious actors. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of differential privacy and Byzantine fault tolerance, providing a practical and secure solution for training machine learning models in decentralized sensor networks. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the privacy budget consumption and the effectiveness of the proposed protocol in mitigating the impact of Byzantine attacks. The system design prioritizes scalability and adaptability, crucial factors for deployment in diverse sensor network scenarios. This work provides a foundational approach for secure and efficient DFL in sensor networks, paving the way for innovative applications in areas such as environmental monitoring, smart cities, and industrial IoT.

title: Provable Program Abstraction and Formal Verification
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to software development focusing on verifiable program abstraction. The core idea is to automatically generate abstract models of programs using formal logic and subsequently rigorously verify their correctness through formal verification techniques. We leverage dependency type theory to construct a layered abstraction framework, where each layer is subjected to automated theorem proving to ensure its consistency with the original program. The key contribution lies in bridging the gap between program abstraction and formal verification, offering a pathway to automate software validation and enhance software reliability. The methodology employs a dependency-based approach, explicitly modeling program state and relationships, leading to more precise and efficient verification. This work outlines the framework, describes the core mechanisms, and highlights the potential impact on software engineering practices. ---

title: Core Claim: A Novel Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for Structural Optimization
abstract: Structural optimization problems are prevalent in various engineering and design disciplines, demanding efficient solutions to complex geometries. Traditional genetic algorithms (GAs) often rely on fixed search strategies, limiting their ability to effectively handle data variability and complex parameter spaces. This paper introduces a novel adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) designed to dynamically adjust the search direction based on input data characteristics, thereby significantly improving optimization results and reducing search time. The AGA leverages a self-adjusting mechanism that adapts the genetic operators (selection, crossover, mutation) based on a learned representation of the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of numerical experiments, showcasing its superior performance compared to established GAs. This work addresses a critical limitation of traditional GAs – their sensitivity to initial parameterization – and offers a promising approach to tackling intricate structural optimization challenges.

title: On Cognitive Architecture-Based Agent Behavioral Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to agent behavioral modeling based on cognitive architecture. Traditional methods often struggle to accurately represent the complex cognitive processes underlying agent behavior, particularly in scenarios demanding nuanced decision-making. This work proposes a framework utilizing a cognitive architecture – a computational representation of a cognitive system – to simulate agent actions and reactions. The architecture incorporates modules for perception, memory, reasoning, and action, allowing for a more realistic and detailed modeling of agent behavior. The core claim is that such an architecture provides a significant improvement over existing techniques by explicitly addressing the limitations of purely reactive or rule-based systems. This approach allows for the simulation of agent behavior with greater fidelity, offering valuable insights into agent decision-making processes in various environments. The key mechanism involves the construction and utilization of the cognitive architecture, enabling comprehensive behavioral modeling and simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Novel Classical Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar quantum phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. This paper explores a novel classical algorithm for information encoding leveraging quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve enhanced security and the ability to handle more complex quantum states than currently available methods. We propose a system based on the design of a "纠缠锁" structure, utilizing entanglement's unique properties to establish a secure communication channel. The core mechanism revolves around creating and manipulating entangled states to encrypt and decrypt information, presenting a fundamentally different approach to classical cryptography. evidence.abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar quantum phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. This paper explores a novel classical algorithm for information encoding leveraging quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve enhanced security and the ability to handle more complex quantum states than currently available methods. We propose a system based on the design of a "纠缠锁" structure, utilizing entanglement's unique properties to establish a secure communication channel. The core mechanism revolves around creating and manipulating entangled states to encrypt and decrypt information, presenting a fundamentally different approach to classical cryptography. This work addresses the limitations of traditional cryptography by introducing a quantum-based system with the potential for increased robustness and adaptability.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非标准算术框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-standard axiomatic framework for computation centered around quantum entanglement. We propose a system of "entanglement arithmetic" that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate novel computational operations and potentially unlock new mechanisms for quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves the design of a specialized arithmetic system that intrinsically incorporates entanglement, offering a departure from traditional axiomatic approaches. We explore the potential of this framework to enhance computational capabilities and provide a new perspective on the design of quantum algorithms. This work necessitates a rigorous examination of the implications of entanglement within a computational context, focusing on potential benefits and challenges related to algorithm design and computational complexity.

title: Diseño y validación de una encuesta para la percepciones y uso de la inteligencia artificial en la gestión
abstract: Fundamentos: El objetivo fue recopilar información sobre cómo se percibe y utiliza la Inteligencia Artificial en los procesos de gestión, con el fin de identificar oportunidades de mejora y desafíos. La Inteligencia Artificial está transformando la forma en que las empresas operan y toman decisiones, pero su adopción debe ir acompañada de una gestión ética y responsable para maximizar sus beneficios y minimizar los riesgos. Los líderes deben de comprender el potencial como las limitaciones de la Inteligencia Artificial. Métodos: Se realizó estudio en el estado de Coahuila, con un diseño observacional, descriptivo, con una muestra no probabilística por conveniencia, participando 43 directivos de unidades médicas, a los cuales se les aplico una encuesta semiestructurada para valorar la percepción y su uso de la inteligencia artificial por la alta dirección. Resultados: de los participantes, el 39.5% fueron de género femenino y 60.5% masculino, de ellos el 41.9% fueron directores médicos, el 16.3% jefes de servicio, el 9.3% coordinadores clínicos de unidades, el 32.6% supervisores delegacionales. El 95.3% refiere que escucho o leyó acerca de la inteligencia artificial. Conclusiones: Observamos que existen múltiples beneficios al trabajar con la inteligencia artificial, como optimizar los procesos, facilita el trabajo, automatizar los procesos, pero se describen las limitaciones como la resistencia, la falta de interés, la falta de capacitación, el costo y la infraestructura de las unidades, pero se presentan una percepción positiva por parte de los directivos con respecto al uso de la inteligencia artificial para el área laboral.

title: SciRep: A Ranking-Aware Representation Model for Scientific Text
abstract: Existing scientific text representation methods based on contrastive learning typically adopt a binary classification paradigm of positive and negative samples, which struggles to capture the complex, hierarchical semantic similarity relationships inherent in scientific texts. To address this, we propose SciRep, a novel two-stage ranking distillation framework. In the first stage, we distill knowledge from a large language model to a medium-scale representation model using generated ranking samples; in the second stage, a multi-teacher strategy further transfers fine-grained ranking capability to a lightweight model. Evaluated on a scientific literature semantic embedding benchmark comprising three tasks, SciRep outperforms the strongest baseline by 11.3% in terms of Average Rank and also achieves the highest Mean Reciprocal Rank scores across all three tasks. These results demonstrate that the proposed ranking-aware distillation mechanism significantly enhances scientific text representation quality while maintaining efficient inference, offering a more effective contrastive learning method for domain-specific retrieval tasks.

title: Population-Calibrated Graph Screening at 835-Million-Address Scale, with Label-Free Transfer to New Chains
abstract: Compliance screening of blockchain addresses is, in practice, a lookup against sanctions registries plus clustering heuristics; it fails on unlabelled addresses and on chains with no label coverage at all. We describe a deployed system that scores an address by its position in a multi-chain transaction graph rather than by its presence in a list. The substrate is a single graph of 835,330,427 addresses and 15,826,261,934 edges across five EVM chains; a shared inductive encoder with per-chain normalisation feeds two scoring heads. Decision thresholds are exact quantiles of the score distribution over the full population, scanned per chain segment, so the alert volume is known in advance. We report: label-free transfer: heads trained on two chains recall 0.8598 / 0.8182 / 0.9967 of held-out positives on Base, Arbitrum and Gnosis at a $10^{-3}$ population alert rate, with no target-chain labels in head training; a static lead-time replay over 68 external registry events: 40 of 68 (58.8%) flagged at the 0.1% budget, $\times$152 over an event-level random-flagging baseline, with first on-chain appearance a median of 528.8 days (Ethereum) / 647.8 days (Tron) before public designation; a serving path whose score is bit-identical to the offline artefact at end-to-end p50 151 ms, gated by a 2,882-address drift panel; and an adversarial harness of eight recurrent reinforcement-learned archetypes that passes an 8-criterion degeneracy audit and, on a detector-independent snapshot, exposes a measured blind spot of the deployed heads against synthesised behaviour.

title: Towards Zero-Shot Transfer Across Embodiments For Driving VLAs
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential in autonomous driving by leveraging multimodal pretraining for instruction following, visual reasoning, and scene-level generalization. In robotic manipulation, scaling VLA fine-tuning across multiple robot setups--especially when unifying representations across embodiments--has been shown to improve in-dataset performance and cross-embodiment generalization; in autonomous driving, however, VLAs remain largely trained on individual datasets and are rarely evaluated for zero-shot transfer to unseen datasets and camera rigs; furthermore naively adding more datasets to the training data does not necessarily lead to better performance within seen embodiments. To address these problems, we study multi-dataset training for the driving task and BEV-Forcing, an auxiliary objective that transfers ground-plane object-layout information from a specialized Bird's-Eye-View model into the VLA backbone. By encouraging the model to represent object position through a shared BEV spatial interface, we show that an auxiliary task such as BEV-Forcing can improve both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance when training on a small number of camera rigs. As the number of training embodiments increases, however, the benefits of the auxiliary task are reduced; we present this as evidence that new techniques in the literature may see their benefits diminish when simply scaling up training diversity, which motivates presenting results taking into account data scaling.

title: Embedding Linear Codes into Optimal Self-Orthogonal Codes Based on Constraint-Preserving Genetic Algorithms
abstract: We study the problem of finding shortest self-orthogonal embeddings of a given code which have the largest possible minimum distance by employing a constraint-preserving genetic algorithm. We show that the orthogonal group is generated by transvections corresponding to weight-four vectors. Using this result together with the fact that all shortest self-orthogonal embeddings can be obtained through the action of the orthogonal group, we construct a genetic algorithm in which each chromosome is represented by a sequence of weight-four vectors. Applying our algorithm to codes with dimensions $9\le k\le 15$ and lengths $22\le n\le 256$, we obtain 280 inequivalent optimal self-orthogonal codes. In particular, we obtain 34 codes with new parameters and 100 codes which are inequivalent to previously known codes with the same parameters.

title: Beyond Context Windows: Persistent Discovery Context for Data-Centric Agents
abstract: Data-centric agents repeatedly perform a discovery step before planning or execution: identifying the data objects relevant to a task. Yet successful discovery outcomes are typically discarded rather than reused. We introduce persistent discovery context, a lightweight memory layer that stores prior intent-to-object mappings and reuses them to augment future retrieval. Across three structured data environments, persistent discovery context consistently improves retrieval quality over metadata-only search, remains effective with automatically generated memories, and exposes a reproducible interference failure mode. In lexically sparse domains, memory-only retrieval can even outperform metadata-based retrieval. These findings suggest that discovery outcomes constitute a useful form of reusable context for data-centric agents.

title: Restoring sparsity in potts machines via mean-field constraints
abstract: Abstract Ising machines and related probabilistic hardware have emerged as promising platforms for NP-hard optimization and sampling. However, many practical problems involve constraints that induce dense or all-to-all couplings, undermining scalability and hardware efficiency. We address this constraint-induced density through two complementary approaches. First, we introduce a hardware-aware native formulation for multi-state probabilistic digits (p-dits) that avoids the locally dense intra-variable couplings required by binary Ising encodings. We validate p-dit dynamics by reproducing known critical behavior of the 2D Potts model. Second, we propose mean-field constraints (MFC), a hybrid scheme that replaces dense pairwise constraint couplings with dynamically updated single-node biases. Applied to balanced graph partitioning, MFC achieves solution quality comparable to exact all-to-all constraint formulations while dramatically reducing graph density. Finally, we demonstrate the practical impact of restored sparsity through an FPGA implementation. In comparisons using FPGA kernel time and CPU solver-loop time, and excluding the current prototype’s host-device schedule-transfer overhead, the FPGA reaches the 50% success threshold more than an order of magnitude faster than the CPU probabilistic solvers and more than two orders of magnitude faster than the Tabu Ising baseline. Together, these results outline a pathway for scaling constrained optimization on probabilistic hardware.

title: Graph-Oriented Context for Prediction and Classification Based on Zipf's Law
abstract: This paper presents a graph-based approach for natural language prediction and text classification using statistical and positional properties derived from Zipf's Law. The proposed method represents tokens according to their occurrences in a global corpus sequence and constructs deterministic graphs to restrict the search space for next-token prediction. Token frequency, positional distance, and contextual relevance are combined to prioritize less frequent tokens and progressively reduce candidate positions. The same representation is applied to text classification through a Zipf-based similarity function using positional and frequency-based weights. Experiments were conducted using a Brazilian Portuguese ICD-10 corpus and a corpus of public funding-call descriptions. The prediction experiments achieved 100% accuracy for evaluated sequences whose tokens belonged to the model vocabulary, while the classification method produced contextually relevant rankings. The results suggest that positional and frequency-based graphs can provide a compact deterministic mechanism for contextual search and may complement Transformer-based Large Language Models by pre-selecting candidate tokens during decoding, potentially reducing the search space and computational requirements.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Storage
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a tantalizing pathway toward revolutionary information storage. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement to create a novel information storage system, leveraging the unique properties of entangled states for enhanced storage density and retrieval speed compared to conventional approaches. We investigate the design of a quantum storage device based on "entanglement resonance," proposing a paradigm shift in data encoding and access. The core claim is that this system overcomes limitations of existing technologies, promising a significant leap forward in information handling. We detail the fundamental principles, mechanism, and potential implications of this approach, highlighting the challenges and future directions for research and development.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Regularization for Enhanced Robustness
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in computational paradigms, offering the potential to surpass classical algorithms in complex data analysis and modeling. This paper investigates the application of adaptive regularization, a key component of QML, to improve the robustness and generalization of machine learning models. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm designed to dynamically adjust model parameters and structure based on data characteristics, specifically focusing on mitigating noise and capturing non-linear relationships. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum properties to achieve a more nuanced and adaptable learning process. The algorithm's proposed adaptive regularization offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, promising to enhance model performance in real-world scenarios.

title: ЖАСАНДЫ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ ЖӘНЕ МАШИНАЛЫҚ АУДАРМА
abstract: Бұл мақалада жасанды интеллект пен машиналық аударманың даму ерекшеліктері, теориялық негіздері және қазіргі заманғы тілдік технологиялардағы рөлі қарастырылады. Машиналық аударманың эволюциясы, нейрондық желілерге негізделген модельдердің тиімділігі және олардың көптілді коммуникацияны жетілдірудегі маңызы талданады. Сонымен қатар, машиналық аударманың артықшылықтары мен шектеулері, сапаны бағалау мәселелері және болашақ даму бағыттары қамтылады. Зерттеу нәтижелері жасанды интеллект технологияларының тілдік кедергілерді азайтудағы әлеуетін көрсетеді.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Deep Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive neural network deep learning framework designed to enhance the scalability and adaptability of deep learning models. Traditional deep learning methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to effectively handle complex data. Our framework dynamically adjusts neural network layer counts and connection weights, enabling the model to adapt to diverse input characteristics and improve performance across a broader range of tasks. The core mechanism relies on a self-tuning parameter strategy, optimizing network structure for specific data patterns. This approach addresses the limitations of static parameter settings, resulting in a more robust and versatile deep learning solution.

title: Multi-Modal Collaborative Reasoning Probabilistic Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for multi-modal collaborative reasoning, centered around the construction of probabilistic models capable of integrating information from diverse modalities such as images, text, and audio. The core of this approach lies in establishing probabilistic dependencies between modalities using Bayesian Networks or Variational Inference techniques. These models incorporate joint probability distributions to facilitate reasoning while explicitly addressing uncertainty inherent in multi-modal data. The research focuses on modeling the interactive relationships between modalities and handling information uncertainty, representing a significant advancement in probabilistic reasoning within complex, multi-sensory environments. The key contribution is a structured methodology for building these models, providing a foundation for applications in areas like intelligent assistance, automated diagnosis, and advanced understanding of human-environment interactions. The proposed framework offers a robust approach to reasoning under uncertainty, leveraging the strengths of multiple modalities to achieve more accurate and reliable conclusions.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive quantum algorithm designed to enhance computational efficiency and accuracy by dynamically adjusting quantum computation processes in response to fluctuations in the quantum potential. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their scalability and adaptability. Our proposed algorithm leverages the inherent dynamics of the quantum potential to continuously refine the computation, enabling faster convergence and improved results. This research focuses on a mechanism that intelligently adapts quantum circuits based on the evolution of the quantum system's state. We present a framework for evaluating and adjusting parameters to optimize performance across a range of input parameters.

title: Title: Bayesian Temporal Dynamics with Adaptive Ensemble Learning (BTAD-AE)
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Temporal Dynamics with Adaptive Ensemble Learning (BTAD-AE), a novel framework for dynamic Bayesian inference in the context of temporal data. Traditional Bayesian methods often face challenges with long-term dependencies and require extensive retraining, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios. BTAD-AE addresses these limitations through a dynamically adaptive ensemble learning approach. The core mechanism centers around a Bayesian update rule that intelligently adjusts ensemble size and weighting based on observed data and prior uncertainty, incorporating a 'temporal memory' to capture evolving temporal dynamics. This allows the system to continuously adapt to changing patterns and improve predictive accuracy over time. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation demonstrating the superior performance of BTAD-AE compared to existing approaches, particularly in scenarios with complex temporal dependencies.

title: Channel-Calibrated Harmonic Entanglement Certificates Under Loss and Phase Noise
abstract: We study the survival of phase-sensitive entanglement in a two-mode-squeezed pair under local Gaussian noise and pair-phase randomization. For the preparation-then-additive model with independent single-quadrature diffusion, we derive an exact Gaussian criterion: in the convention [q,p]=i and vacuum variance 1/2, the state is NPT if and only if d_+ d_- < sinh^2(2r). For unequal thermal attenuators followed by an arbitrary circular phase law with characteristic coefficients chi_d, a locally filtered Fock block has a negative eigenvalue if and only if |chi_d| > tau^d, with tau determined by the output occupations, anomalous coherence, and determinant of the filtered Gaussian core. This provides a sufficient certificate of full-state NPT and one-copy distillability, but not a complete infinite-dimensional PPT criterion. The analysis identifies finite-order harmonic blind spots, a composable detectability radius under independent phase noise, and calibration rules based on number-resolved coherences. We also give a time-ordered Lyapunov treatment of simultaneous squeezing and diffusion and a conditional de Sitter-to-observable transfer protocol whose interpretation depends on the specified bath, mode basis, transfer functions, and detector likelihood.
