title: ORB-SVM : An Innovative Hybrid Framework for Efficient Brain Tumor Detection from MRI Scans
abstract: Brain cancer remains one of the most significant challenges in modern medicine, where the accuracy of early stage diagnosis is a decisive factor in patient survival and treatment efficacy. Although Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the established gold standard for visualizing neurological structures, the interpretation of these high dimensional scans is often complicated by subjective variability among practitioners and the inherent noise present in complex medical images. While contemporary approaches frequently rely on high parameter deep learning architectures, such models often involve significant computational costs and require extensive data for effective training. This study introduces a hybrid framework that utilizes the Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) algorithm for precise feature extraction and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification [1], [2]. The proposed approach achieves a sub- stantial data reduction of approximately 99.5%, which effectively minimizes the influence of non informative background data while preserving critical diagnostic patterns essential for tumor identification. By balancing feature sparsity with a robust kernel based classifier, this methodology addresses the limitations of over parameterized systems while maintaining high diagnostic integrity. Experimental evaluations conducted on the Br35H dataset demonstrate that the framework attains a classification accuracy of 97.5%. The findings suggest that the integration of localized feature representation and optimized classification provides a reliable and resource efficient alternative for medical image analysis, offering a structured solution that maintains per- formance without the need for extensive computational overhead.

title: Semantic Signal-Assisted Inspection and Recovery Allocation in Reverse Logistics
abstract: Reverse-logistics operators often decide how to inspect and route returned assets before their condition is fully observed, while full inspection consumes scarce labor. Semantic Signal-Assisted Decision Support converts return notes into a condition factor and a signal-quality score that guide inspection depth and recovery allocation under shared labor capacity. We evaluate the framework in three synthetic benchmark scenarios spanning information technology decommissioning, aircraft maintenance, and consumer-electronics returns. Across 30 paired simulation seeds, the keyword implementation improves net recovery value relative to a structured-feature comparator with noisy full inspection while reducing inspection cost in all three scenarios. A risk-blind comparator that skips inspection altogether still records higher value under the benchmark's purely economic objective. At matched inspection cost, score-guided targeting adds 53.9 thousand United States dollars per batch in the aircraft scenario but has little economic effect in the other two configurations; phrase and large language model extractors provide further gains in the aircraft scenario. These results show how narrative evidence can support inspection allocation before recovery decisions are made.

title: Bio-Information Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize bio-information processing, specifically focusing on enhancing biological signal detection and decoding. Traditional methods in bioinformatics often rely on classical algorithms, which struggle to effectively capture and analyze subtle variations within complex biological systems. We propose a novel theoretical framework incorporating quantum entanglement, utilizing a specially designed quantum sensor to detect minute changes in biological signals. This approach offers a fundamentally new pathway for improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy. The core claim is that this quantum entanglement-based approach provides significantly enhanced sensitivity and precision compared to existing bio-information processing techniques. The research will investigate the principles of entanglement, its potential applications within biological systems, and the development of a prototype quantum sensor for real-world testing. This paper outlines the theoretical basis, proposed mechanism, and initial experimental considerations for this groundbreaking investigation.

title: Title: Topology-Enhanced Quantum Algorithm Verification
abstract: Quantum algorithms promise revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, yet their verification remains a significant challenge. Traditional verification methods often rely on exhaustive testing, which is computationally expensive and impractical for complex algorithms. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging topological concepts to proactively identify potential errors and vulnerabilities within quantum algorithms, significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of the verification process. This work details the development of a method for analyzing the topological structure of quantum circuits, identifying anomalous regions indicative of errors, and ultimately providing a more robust verification framework. We introduce a novel topological analysis technique that incorporates the principles of graph theory and measure theory to effectively assess algorithm integrity. The core claim is that this method enhances the accuracy of quantum algorithm verification by detecting subtle errors that traditional approaches miss. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the proposed method, including detailed mathematical formulations, illustrative examples, and a discussion of its potential impact on the future of quantum algorithm verification. The focus is on providing a practical, mathematically grounded solution to a critical problem within the quantum realm.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Simulating Complex Biological Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the use of probabilistic programming as a powerful tool for modeling and simulating complex biological systems. Current simulation methods frequently employ overly simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to accurately represent the inherent uncertainty present in biological processes. Probabilistic programming offers a framework for explicitly incorporating prior knowledge, rigorously quantifying uncertainty, and conducting sensitivity analysis, ultimately leading to more realistic and informative simulations. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the expressive power of probabilistic programming languages to define complex models where variables are represented as probability distributions, allowing for the simulation of systems under various conditions and the assessment of potential outcomes. This work outlines the key benefits, demonstrates the fundamental concepts, and highlights the potential impact of this methodology on various domains within biological research.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Uncertainty
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) offers a powerful approach to discovering mathematical relationships from data. However, its efficacy is often limited by the exponential growth of the search space, leading to brittle and unreliable expressions. This paper introduces a hierarchical symbolic regression algorithm incorporating Bayesian inference to mitigate these challenges. The system decomposes the regression problem into a hierarchy of subproblems, allowing for focused exploration. Bayesian methods are employed to quantify uncertainty at each stage, guiding the search towards more robust and generalizable expressions. This approach demonstrates improved scalability and reliability compared to standard SR methods, particularly when dealing with complex, high-dimensional systems. The core contribution lies in the integration of hierarchical decomposition with Bayesian uncertainty quantification for a more effective and stable discovery process.

title: Explainable Adversarial Generative Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to building explainable adversarial generative models. The core claim is to construct models capable of interpreting the process of generating adversarial samples, thereby enhancing the trustworthiness and security of generative models. The proposed mechanism integrates adversarial training with explainable AI techniques, specifically focusing on tracing the generation path of adversarial samples and analyzing the influential factors. Current generative models often operate as black boxes, making it difficult to understand how adversarial examples are created and how to defend against them. This work addresses this critical gap by providing a framework for understanding and mitigating the risks posed by adversarial attacks. The resulting models offer increased robustness and provide insights into vulnerabilities within the generative process. The primary objective is to move beyond simply detecting adversarial attacks to truly understanding *why* they succeed, ultimately leading to more secure and reliable generative models. The key contribution lies in the combined approach of adversarial training and explainable AI, offering a pathway toward more transparent and controllable generative systems.

The core claim is to construct models capable of interpreting the process of generating adversarial samples, thereby enhancing the trustworthiness and security of generative models. The proposed mechanism integrates adversarial training with explainable AI techniques, specifically focusing on tracing the generation path of adversarial samples and analyzing the influential factors. Current generative models often operate as black boxes, making it difficult to understand how adversarial examples are created and how to defend against them. This work addresses this critical gap by providing a framework for understanding and mitigating the risks posed by adversarial attacks. The resulting models offer increased robustness and provide insights into vulnerabilities within the generative process. The primary objective is to move beyond simply detecting adversarial attacks to truly understanding *why* they succeed, ultimately leading to more secure and reliable generative models. The key contribution lies in the combined approach of adversarial training and explainable AI, offering a pathway toward more transparent and controllable generative systems.

title: Dynamic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning within Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) utilizing dynamic programming techniques. Traditional reinforcement learning methods often struggle with the complexity and sample inefficiency inherent in POMDPs. Our proposed algorithm leverages dynamic programming's ability to systematically explore the state space while explicitly accounting for uncertainty, represented through a belief state. This belief state, a probability distribution over possible hidden states, guides the agent's decision-making process, leading to improved sample efficiency and faster convergence compared to standard reinforcement learning methods. The core of the algorithm involves a modified Bellman equation that incorporates the uncertainty represented by the belief state. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, the advantages of this approach, outlining a framework suitable for tackling complex, partially observable environments. The key contributions lie in the integration of dynamic programming with belief state representation, offering a more targeted and effective learning strategy for POMDPs.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Temporal Logic Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic program synthesis that leverages temporal logic constraints for rigorous verification. Traditional program synthesis methods frequently struggle to guarantee correctness when temporal relationships – such as ordering and timing – are involved. Our framework addresses this limitation by integrating temporal logic reasoning directly into the synthesis process. We propose a hybrid architecture comprising neural networks for pattern recognition and a temporal logic engine for verifying and refining synthesized programs against specified temporal requirements. The core innovation lies in providing a formal verification framework, significantly enhancing the reliability of neuro-symbolic program synthesis. We formalize this approach using mathematical notation, outlining the key components and their interactions. The resulting system demonstrates improved accuracy and reliability in generating programs that meet complex temporal constraints, representing a substantial advancement in the field. The proposed method tackles the challenge of temporal reasoning in program synthesis, offering a path towards more dependable and robust automated program generation.

title: Axiomatic Foundation for Explainable AI – Causal Inference as a Requirement
abstract: Current approaches to explainable AI (XAI) frequently fall short of providing genuinely understandable and trustworthy explanations. These methods often rely on post-hoc interpretations of black-box models, which can be misleading due to their failure to capture the underlying causal mechanisms driving predictions. This paper proposes a novel axiomatic foundation for XAI, arguing that true explanation necessitates a thorough understanding of causal relationships. We posit that causal inference represents a fundamental requirement for explainability, moving beyond superficial feature importance or local linear approximations. This framework introduces a rigorous approach to assessing explanations by evaluating their consistency with known causal structures, leading to more robust and reliable explanations. We define key concepts and provide a formal outline for evaluating explanation methods based on their ability to accurately represent and leverage causal knowledge. The core contribution is establishing a clear criterion – causal fidelity – for evaluating XAI methods, ensuring explanations reflect the true causal drivers of model behavior.

title: Simulating Evolution with Coupled Physical Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimization and search problems by integrating evolutionary algorithms with simulated physical systems. The core idea, termed "coupled physical systems," leverages the inherent constraints and dynamics of physical models to guide and refine the search process within evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often suffer from issues such as premature convergence and sensitivity to initial populations. This work addresses these limitations by mapping the search space of the evolutionary algorithm onto a physically relevant system, such as a fluid dynamics simulation or a particle swarm optimization framework. The physical system then acts as a selective filter, pruning the search space based on its own physical laws and behaviors. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual framework, highlighting the potential for improved search efficiency, robustness, and the discovery of optimal solutions. Specifically, we introduce a mathematical formulation for this coupling, outlining the core components and interactions. The framework provides a robust methodology for tackling complex optimization landscapes where traditional methods struggle.

title: 基于动态拓扑的机器学习模型评估
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning model evaluation framework based on dynamic topology, designed to assess model performance in complex environments. Traditional model evaluation methods rely on static models, limiting the potential for robust generalization. This framework leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to provide a more comprehensive and adaptive evaluation strategy, enhancing model robustness and generalization capabilities. We introduce a new method for dynamically characterizing model behavior within a complex, evolving landscape. This approach offers a shift towards a more nuanced and insightful assessment of model performance, particularly when dealing with data that exhibits significant structural changes or dependencies. The proposed framework focuses on quantifying the model's ability to adapt and maintain its performance across diverse conditions. The core mechanism involves the construction of a dynamic topology representation of the model's output space, enabling the identification of critical regions and vulnerabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of carefully selected experiments, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional methods in evaluating models with varying levels of complexity and uncertainty. The results highlight the significant potential of dynamic topology in improving model reliability and adaptability.

title: 基于动态拓扑的全局优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel global optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static or fixed topologies, struggling to effectively handle complex environmental changes. Our algorithm employs a dynamic topology structure that adjusts throughout the optimization process, allowing for adaptive and robust solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several case studies, showcasing its ability to navigate challenging scenarios and achieve superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The core mechanism involves the continuous manipulation of the topology to facilitate the exploration of the solution space.

title: Graph Generative Adversarial Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used to represent and reason about complex information. A significant challenge in KG management is incompleteness, where many potential relationships between entities remain unobserved. Traditional KG completion methods often rely on statistical inference or embedding techniques, which may struggle to capture complex relational patterns. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Graph Generative Adversarial Networks (GANS) to address this challenge. We introduce a generator network that generates new triples (si, rj, ok) and a discriminator network that assesses the likelihood of these generated triples based on the existing KG structure. The generator and discriminator engage in an adversarial training process, where the generator attempts to produce realistic triples that fool the discriminator, while the discriminator strives to distinguish between real and generated triples. Our approach leverages the GAN framework to learn complex relational patterns and enhance the completeness of the KG. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and outline potential future directions. The key contribution lies in applying GANs to the inherently relational problem of KG completion, offering a potentially more powerful and flexible solution compared to existing techniques.

title: Fabrication on absent fields: a pre-registered six-arm document-extraction bake-off (round 1)
abstract: Complete public artifact of a pre-registered document-extraction bake-off: six extraction setups (Velrim’s included — Velrim ran the comparison and sells one of the six) over 124 real documents, scored under an analysis plan frozen and published before the first paid call. Headline measurement: fabrication on absent fields — pooled across the six setups, 17% of the fields absent from the document came back with an invented value. The archive holds the frozen analysis plan, golden sets and probe set, every raw per-field output with request IDs, per-repeat scores, figures, the disclosure register, and the scoring CLI (velrim-eval); re-scoring the published outputs needs no keys and costs nothing. Code is Apache-2.0; source corpora carry their own licenses (CC BY 4.0 / MIT), attributed in the archive. Write-up: velrim.com/research/fabrication-on-absent-fields — living repository: github.com/velrimhq/velrim-eval.

title: Robust UAV Detection and Classification in Noisy RF Environments via Multimodal CNN-Based IQ and Spectrogram Fusion
abstract: This study aims to autonomously detect and classify Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), which are becoming increasingly widespread, based on their emitted radio frequency (RF) signals in highly noisy and interference-prone RF environments where traditional optical and radar-based methods prove insufficient. The dataset used in this study is the “Noisy Drone RF Signal Classification” dataset, which consists of seven classes in total—six different drone models and one noise class—and is balanced across classes. As the methodological approach, a multimodal hybrid deep learning (DL) architecture was developed, integrating raw time-domain IQ signals (1D-CNN) with frequency-domain spectrogram representations (2D-CNN). To enhance model performance and generalization capability, techniques such as Batch Normalization, Dropout, Label Smoothing, and Gradient Clipping were incorporated into the architecture. The model was trained using the AdamW optimization algorithm alongside a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler. In order to efficiently process large-scale datasets, memory management optimizations including memory-mapped files (mmap) and lazy loading were implemented. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multimodal model achieves an accuracy of 87.42% and an F1-score of 0.87, indicating strong detection performance. SNR-based analyses reveal that the model achieves accuracy levels ranging between 64.52% and 82.40% under negative-SNR conditions (−20 to 0 dB), while exceeding 89% accuracy under positive-SNR conditions. The findings indicate that multimodal DL approaches can achieve high performance in UAV detection and classification even in noisy RF environments.

title: Social federated learning (SFL): Leveraging shared data to boost learning performance
abstract: Collaboration between edge devices has the potential to scale up machine learning (ML) by enabling access to unprecedented amounts of data. Federated learning (FL) is a collaborative algorithm in which clients learn from each other without sharing private data. However, edge devices tend to have different data distributions because they are naturally exposed to different data sources. This heterogeneity, also known as non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, has been shown to decrease the accuracy of FL. We study how limited data sharing among users can alleviate this performance degradation. Such sharing can occur naturally on a social graph or be incentivized by the platform. We evaluated the performance gains of data sharing on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 across topologies including complete graphs, clusters, and stochastic block models. We empirically demonstrate that modest data sharing between neighbors on a social graph enhances learning performance in the non-IID case. Interestingly, we found that data sharing could also improve performance in the IID case. By normalizing the dataset sizes, we verified that this boost is significant even if sharing does not increase the number of data points per client. Therefore, data sharing is an efficient technique for improving social federated learning (SFL).

title: SecDT: A Profile-Based Security Layer for TRDP Communications
abstract: The Train Real-time Data Protocol (TRDP) is widely used on rolling stock but it provides limited native support for cryptographic protection. Furthermore, the multicast traffic profile used in TRDP Process Data to exchange critical information between onboard subsystems makes the introduction of cryptographic protection a challenge. This paper presents a lightweight security layer for secure TRDP communication that implements a number of security profiles built around modern cryptographic algorithms. This additional layer relies on an On-board Key Management System (OKMS) for both security profile negotiation, dynamic key distribution and key lifecycle management. The security profiles allow for cryptographic agility and flexibility, ranging from simple authentication to Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) algorithms. The security profile negotiation procedure guarantees all TRDP End Devices (ED) on a common Communication ID (ComID) share the same security profile and can therefore process each other's messages. A prototype implementation based on mbedTLS and Arm Platform Security Architecture (PSA) was developed and evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate manageable overhead, suitable for the real-time and time-sensitive communication found on rolling stock.

title: Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as economic agents, yet there is little evidence whether LLM agents are suited for participating in market mechanisms designed for humans, and whether these mechanisms deliver desired outcomes when faced with LLM agents. We address this question by replicating seminal economic experiments, replacing human subjects with LLM agents. We place agents in a double auction environment, which is a widely-used market mechanism. We check whether such a market is able to deliver an efficient allocation of resources, thereby testing a novel dimension of alignment of LLM agents -- their compatibility with a fundamental market mechanism. We find that markets populated by LLM agents exhibit slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium, thus providing less efficient allocations than markets populated by humans. We then analyze agents' individual trading decisions and find substantial heterogeneity both across model families and market roles. We also run a lexical analysis of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces generated by the agents. We find that the decision to execute a trade rather than continue incrementally adjusting prices is associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency. We publicly release our testing framework, which can be used for future evaluations.

title: New binary optimal LCD codes using heuristic embedding
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the construction of binary optimal LCD codes through short LCD embeddings. For this purpose, we design heuristic frameworks based on a greedy algorithm. We explore the search spaces of LCD embeddings using the fact that an invertible matrix together with an arbitrary matrix yields an LCD embedding. We therefore use elementary row operations on the invertible block and single entry-flips on the arbitrary block as local moves in a greedy algorithm. Using this method, we have found $14$ optimal new LCD codes with dimensions 7 and 8 for lengths from 55 to 201.

title: Masking a Field's Loss Does Not Isolate That Field
abstract: Masking a field's loss does not isolate that field. Five LoRA runs on a 0.6B guard model. Runs 1-2 show a masked output field moving anyway. Runs 3-5 add a three-arm target-module ablation: attention-only and MLP-only are disjoint and each independently destroys the model's third severity class, so retargeting the adapter is not available as a repair. A documented operator control becomes a silent no-op.

title: Information Entropy Calculation & Quantum Topology
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum topology to information entropy calculation, presenting a novel algorithm that leverages this structure for enhanced computational efficiency. We propose a quantum computation framework centered around "information encoding-decoding," aiming to significantly improve compression and communication strategies. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum topological properties to build a more efficient and robust system for information processing. The paper details the algorithm's design, the theoretical underpinnings of the quantum topology approach, and preliminary results demonstrating potential improvements over existing methods. The investigation considers the implications of this approach for understanding fundamental information theory and its applications in data compression and secure communication.

title: Dynamic Entropy-Based Machine Learning Model (DEBM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model, the Dynamic Entropy-Based Machine Learning Model (DEBM), that leverages the concept of entropy to dynamically adjust model parameters and enhance its adaptability to changing data. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static parameters, limiting their ability to effectively learn from evolving datasets. The DEBM addresses this limitation by incorporating an entropy-based mechanism that continuously monitors and adjusts model parameters based on data fluctuations, resulting in a more robust and adaptive learning process. The paper details the model's architecture, the entropy-driven adjustment process, and its potential applications across various machine learning domains. We present preliminary results demonstrating the model's effectiveness in handling complex data patterns and achieving superior performance compared to traditional approaches.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Neural Network Weight Initialization
abstract: Traditional methods for initializing weights in neural networks, such as Xavier and He initialization, rely on statistical assumptions about the distribution of network activations. These assumptions often fail to capture the complex dynamics of deep learning, leading to suboptimal performance and slower convergence. This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network weight initialization inspired by quantum mechanics. We leverage concepts like superposition and tunneling to explore a wider range of potential weight values, effectively broadening the search space for the optimal initialization. The core idea is to treat the weight initialization problem as a quantum exploration process, where weights are represented as quantum states and the optimization process involves manipulating these states. We introduce a mathematical framework based on probability amplitudes and phase functions to model this quantum exploration. title: Quantum Topologies for Adaptive Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topologies, a novel approach to quantum computing, offers a unique framework for algorithm optimization. This paper explores the application of quantum topologies to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters, thereby achieving enhanced performance. We introduce a self-optimizing algorithm that leverages quantum state evolution to automatically tune parameters, offering a significant advancement over traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers around quantum state manipulation to achieve real-time parameter adjustments, resulting in improved efficiency.

title: Causal Discovery from Interventional and Observational Data using Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of integrating interventional and observational data to enhance the accuracy and robustness of causal discovery algorithms. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely solely on observational data, which may be biased due to confounding variables or unobserved confounders. This research proposes a novel approach by leveraging Bayesian networks, allowing for the explicit modeling of causal relationships derived from both experimental (interventional) and observational data. The core claim is that combining these data sources can significantly improve the identification of true causal structures. The mechanism involves utilizing Bayesian networks to represent the probabilistic dependencies between variables, incorporating interventions to directly measure causal effects alongside observational measurements. We explore the theoretical underpinnings and discuss the potential benefits and challenges of this integrated approach, highlighting its advantages over existing techniques. We demonstrate that incorporating interventional data can resolve ambiguities and improve the accuracy of discovered causal graphs, particularly in scenarios with complex confounding. The primary contribution of this work is a framework for robust causal discovery that accounts for both the strength and direction of causal influences.

title: Artificial Intelligent (AI) and Endangered Language Preservation: Challenges Among Igbo, Hausa and Yoruba
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligent (AI) is geared recently into a diverse array of innovative tools that empowered linguistic communities to document, preserve, and share endangered languages. Considering the inherent complexities of linguistics, technical limitations, and ethical consideration on human system as an assessing long-term sustainability of language preservation, a focus on AI-driven tools in preserving endangered language rears. This study specifically aims to explore AI preservative potentials in preserving endangered languages specifically the cultural and linguistic subtleties, such as nuances of expression and idiomatic phrases, that define endangered languages among the three major ethnics languages in Nigeria. To systematically draw strings of inferences on that, a cross-sectional research design and quota sampling technique was adopted. 45 married men and women (15 each) from the 3 major ethnic group (Igbo, Hausa, and Yoruba) in Nigeria were sampled using structured questionnaire. They comprised 22 male and 23 females with age ranges from 39 to 67 years (M = 51.5, SD = 7.17). Descriptive statistics was used for data analysis. The findings identified the widely used AI driven tools across the three tribes in Nigeria; its potential; and technical challenges. It builds on multi-agent Ai frame work and argue that AI can identify, translate, and interpret nuances and tonal subtleties of languages if technological resources, concise computational methods are constituted. Keywords: Artificial Intelligent; Endangered language preservation; Nigeria

title: Self-Adaptive Topology of Quantum Entanglement Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive topology to quantum entanglement analysis, aiming to refine the measurement process and improve the accuracy of entanglement characterization. Traditional approaches often rely on static models, limiting the ability to dynamically adjust the analysis based on the system's state. We propose a novel method that leverages the inherent properties of self-adaptive topology to enhance entanglement analysis. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically modifying the topology during the entanglement measurement, thereby minimizing noise and maximizing the fidelity of the measurement. The resulting system exhibits improved performance in analyzing complex entangled states, demonstrating a significant advancement in the precision of quantum entanglement characterization.

title: Adaptive-Adaptive Bayesian Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive-adaptive Bayesian modeling framework designed to enhance predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities. Traditional model parameterization methods often struggle to adapt to evolving data patterns, leading to suboptimal performance. Our approach leverages an adaptive learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on data, minimizing overfitting and maximizing predictive effectiveness. We present a novel methodology incorporating Bayesian inference and adaptive parameter updates, demonstrating significant improvements in prediction consistency and robustness across a range of datasets. The core mechanism centers on a hierarchical Bayesian model, allowing for flexible representation of uncertainty and enabling more informed parameter selection. This work addresses a critical challenge in machine learning by providing a robust and adaptable solution for complex data analysis.

title: Quantum State Dynamics: A Novel Modeling Approach for Enhanced Computational Precision
abstract: Quantum state dynamics represents a paradigm shift in the field of quantum information processing, offering unprecedented control over quantum systems. This paper explores a novel modeling approach, leveraging dynamic topology transformations, to enhance the precision of quantum state representations. We introduce a framework wherein the inherent topology of a quantum state is continuously adjusted through a series of transformations, allowing for a more accurate representation of the system's behavior. This approach overcomes limitations of static models by dynamically adapting to complex quantum environments. The core mechanism focuses on the iterative adjustment of topology, achieving a significant improvement in computational fidelity compared to traditional methods. The results demonstrate the efficacy of this methodology in modeling various quantum systems, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum algorithm design and error mitigation.

title: Core Claim: Developing a quantum topological vulnerability assessment method, leveraging quantum state topology to evaluate the vulnerability of quantum systems to quantum attacks, and discovering quantum security strategies.
abstract: Quantum computing has rapidly advanced, presenting both immense opportunities and significant challenges. Quantum attacks, exploiting vulnerabilities in quantum systems, pose a serious threat to current cryptographic protocols and essential technologies. Current vulnerability assessment methods are largely based on classical algorithms, often lacking the ability to accurately predict and mitigate these attacks. This research introduces a novel quantum topological vulnerability assessment framework, utilizing quantum state topology to comprehensively evaluate the susceptibility of quantum systems to various attacks. The framework employs a sophisticated approach that exploits the inherent topological properties of quantum states to identify and quantify potential weaknesses. The core of the method involves constructing a quantum state representation that encodes the system's topology and dynamically assesses this representation to identify vulnerabilities. This assessment is then compared against known attack scenarios, leading to the discovery of quantum security strategies. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through simulations and preliminary experimental results, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the robustness of quantum systems. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to quantum security evaluation, offering a more precise and adaptable method compared to existing techniques.

title: Quantum Back-Erasing Reconstruction and Control
abstract: This paper investigates the reconstruction and control of quantum decoherence through a novel approach of inverse back-erasure. Traditional decoherence control strategies primarily focus on mitigating the effects of environmental noise, often employing passive shielding or error correction techniques. This work proposes a proactive method utilizing feedback control to actively reverse the decoherence process, thereby enhancing the coherence of quantum states. The core concept involves precisely measuring the quantum system's interaction with its environment and applying corrective actions to counteract the detrimental effects of decoherence. We explore theoretical frameworks based on Hamiltonian engineering and feedback control theory, formulating a mathematical model for the system and outlining the control strategy. The central equation governing the process is: Δψ(t+Δt) = α(t) Δψ(t) + β(t) (H - η(t) ⋅ H') Δψ(t) where Δψ(t+Δt) is the quantum state at time t+Δt, α(t) is the decoherence factor, β(t) is the control factor, H is the Hamiltonian of the system, H' is the environmental Hamiltonian, and η(t) is the feedback control term. The goal is to manipulate β(t) and η(t) to minimize the effect of decoherence. The effectiveness of this approach is discussed in terms of coherence time extension and entanglement preservation. The research contributes a new paradigm for quantum control, offering potential advancements in quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum sensing. ---

title: Quantum Mechanics Principle-Based Parallel Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel parallel computing architecture grounded in the principles of quantum mechanics. The core concept involves leveraging quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to construct a quantum bit (qubit)-based parallel computing system, thereby facilitating the concurrent execution of complex computational tasks. The architecture aims to significantly enhance computational efficiency compared to classical parallel computing approaches. This document outlines the theoretical framework, key architectural components, and potential operational principles of this system. It explores the challenges and opportunities presented by implementing such a system and highlights the potential for transformative advancements in fields reliant on computationally intensive tasks, such as drug discovery, materials science, and artificial intelligence.

title: Symbolic Simulation of Complex Systems using Neural Networks
abstract: The increasing complexity of real-world systems – ranging from financial markets to biological networks – poses a significant challenge to traditional simulation methods. Conventional simulation techniques, such as differential equations and agent-based modeling, often struggle to capture the emergent behavior arising from intricate interactions. Neural networks offer a promising alternative due to their ability to learn complex patterns from data. However, their inherent "black-box" nature limits their utility in systems requiring interpretability, transparency, and precise control. This paper proposes a novel hybrid approach to complex system simulation, integrating neural networks with symbolic simulation. The core idea is to utilize a neural network to approximate the dynamics of the system, while simultaneously maintaining a symbolic representation for understanding and controlling the simulation. This hybrid approach aims to combine the predictive power of neural networks with the interpretability and controllability of symbolic models. The specific formulation involves a neural network trained to predict the state of the system at a given time, based on its current state and input parameters. The output of the neural network is then used to update the symbolic representation, and vice-versa, creating a feedback loop that allows for continuous refinement and adaptation. This process is facilitated by carefully designed loss functions that balance prediction accuracy with symbolic representation fidelity. The paper outlines the key components of this hybrid system and discusses its potential applications across various domains.

title: Multi-Layer Controlled Multi-Output Remote State Preparation of Single-Particle States
abstract: We propose two multi-layer controlled multi-output remote state preparation (RSP) schemes for arbitrary single-qubit and single-qudit states. Twelve-particle entangled channels are constructed in two-dimensional and d-dimensional Hilbert spaces, and a hierarchical authorization mechanism is introduced to enable controllers with different permission levels to jointly and selectively regulate the reconstruction of quantum states at multiple receivers. First, based on a twelve-qubit maximally entangled channel, we design a deterministic three-layer controlled multi-output RSP protocol in which one sender assists three receivers in preparing their respective target single-qubit states. In this protocol, the controllers are assigned high-, medium-, and low-level permissions. Under different multi-layer control conditions, the three receivers can reconstruct their respective original single-qubit states by performing appropriate local unitary operations. The results show that the protocol achieves unit success probability, exhibits good universality and provides a structured basis for extension to larger multi-user settings, and enforces hierarchical access control by preventing unauthorized receivers from deterministically reconstructing the target states. Subsequently, we replace the maximally entangled channel with a non-maximally entangled twelve-qubit state. After the sender performs two specific three-qubit projective measurements, the receivers can probabilistically reconstruct their respective target states under the same three-layer control structure by introducing auxiliary qubits, applying controlled-U gates, and measuring the auxiliary systems. Finally, by employing positive operator-valued measurements, the above scheme is generalized from qubit systems to arbitrary d-dimensional qudit systems, providing a theoretical basis for exploring larger multi-user quantum communication settings with hierarchical authorization.

title: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization
abstract: Occupation-Space Variational Quantum Optimization (OS-VQO) is introduced as a new framework for quantum electronic structure calculations in which the quantum variational object is an occupation state rather than a many-electron wavefunction. Consequently, the quantum processor operates directly on the occupation numbers, the fundamental variational variables of Natural Orbital Functional Theory (NOFT). The framework is realized through a logarithmically scaling qudit encoding of electron-pair occupation spaces and a hierarchical variational circuit that spans the complete physically admissible occupation manifold while enforcing all N-representability constraints by construction. Noiseless quantum simulations and raw executions on IBM Quantum processors for hydrogen systems up to H216 demonstrate excellent agreement without error mitigation or post-processing, constituting, to the best of our knowledge, the largest raw quantum hardware demonstration reported for a strongly correlated electronic structure calculation. These results demonstrate that quantum variational optimization need not rely on many-electron wavefunctions, opening a new direction for quantum electronic structure calculations based on functional theories.

title: Development of a Real-time Solar Panel Power Prediction Model Using the Long Short-term Memory
abstract: Indonesia’s remote islands face significant challenges in electricity access due to the high cost and logistical difficulties of extending the national grid, leading many communities to rely on expensive and polluting diesel generators. Solar-based microgrids offer a sustainable alternative, yet the intermittent nature of solar energy, driven by fluctuating weather conditions, poses major obstacles to a reliable power supply and efficient system sizing. This study addresses these issues by developing a real-time solar panel power prediction model using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. A 50 Wp solar panel system equipped with an INA260 current sensor, a voltage sensor, a DHT-22 temperature sensor, and an ESP32 microcontroller was constructed to collect real-time voltage, current, and temperature data at 10-second intervals. The collected data underwent preprocessing, feature engineering, and transformation into supervised learning sequences for training. Three temporal resolutions of the LSTM model were systematically evaluated: 3-minute, 2-minute, and 1-minute, all with 30 output timesteps. Performance was assessed using rolling-window predictions on the held-out test set with metrics including RMSE, MAPE, and R². Results demonstrated that finer temporal resolution significantly improves forecasting accuracy. The 1-minute variation achieved the best performance with the lowest RMSE and highest R², effectively capturing both diurnal patterns and short-term fluctuations in solar power output. The developed LSTM model enables accurate short-term predictions (30–90 minutes ahead), supporting proactive energy management, including optimized battery charging, load scheduling, and reduced grid dependency. Future work will incorporate additional meteorological variables and seasonal data to improve model robustness further. title: PNFR: practicality-enhanced and non-interactive privacy-preserving federated regressions
abstract: Abstract Federated learning is a technology that is used to protect data privacy in machine learning. Nonetheless, in federated learning, updating the global model requires the use of gradient descent algorithm, which involves multiple rounds of interaction between entities to complete the iterative updates, inevitably incurring massive computational and communication overhead. In 2020, Wang et al. first proposed a non-interactive federated regression scheme, which effectively improves the training efficiency of regression models while protecting the privacy of local training data. However, like most current federated regressions, it involves a third authority (TA) to generate keys for each entity, which poses a significant privacy risk and results in considerable communication overhead. From the view of security and practicality, this paper first proposes a multi-party homomorphic encryption algorithm named MPaillier. Furthermore, we have designed PNFR, a privacy-preserving federated learning scheme for regressions training built on the MPaillier algorithm. The participating entities of PNFR are the data owners and a cloud server, eliminating the need for a TA, thus enhancing the practicality and efficiency of the scheme. Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme is $\sim 10^{3}$ times faster than interactive federated regressions PrivFL and about 80% faster than non-interactive federated regressions VANE.

Furthermore, we have designed PNFR, a privacy-preserving federated learning scheme for regressions training built on the MPaillier algorithm. The participating entities of PNFR are the data owners and a cloud server, eliminating the need for a TA, thus enhancing the practicality and efficiency of the scheme. Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme is $\sim 10^{3}$ times faster than interactive federated regressions PrivFL and about 80% faster than non-interactive federated regressions VANE.

title: Learning Manipulation-Sufficient Representations via Outcome Bottlenecks
abstract: Networked manipulation endpoints couple perception to actuation across compute- and bandwidth-limited links, yet commonly exchange dense geometric states optimized for fidelity rather than action outcomes. A stochastic representation is learned with a policy-free, action-conditioned outcome bottleneck: marginal outcome log-loss supplies distortion and a KL term regularizes rate. The construction is motivated by the minimal statistic that preserves the outcome distribution of every admissible action, while the implemented finite model is evaluated as a rate-regularized mixture predictor. The same encoder and outcome head support grasp selection, singleton conformal filtering, active viewpoint selection, and latent test-time adaptation. A finite-probe theorem identifies the local level-set tangent space with the null space of an outcome Jacobian. The synthetic oracle verifies this result; on scanned objects, an analytic surrogate agrees with measured simulator invariances within \(0.56^\circ\). Across 11,979 simulated grasps on 13 objects, a reconstructed-geometry wrench score attains 0.542 AUC against lift success and falls below chance on curved objects, while our representation attains 0.876. At 25\% commitment, executed-grasp success is 0.503 versus 0.984. The 512-byte interface is \(288\times\) smaller than one RGB-D frame and runs at 16\,ms per CPU decision. Independent synthetic points track the tested conformal levels; scanned-object all-pair coverage is reported as a clustered empirical diagnostic. On unseen objects, within-scene AUC falls to 0.569, and a full-feedback update raises empirical mean pairwise coverage from 0.728 to 0.883.

title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness & Multi-Domain Reasoning Benchmark (Task Set)
abstract: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness & Multi-Domain Reasoning Benchmark (Task Set)OverviewThis dataset contains a standardized benchmark task set designed to evaluate and probe the faithfulness, deductive reasoning capability, and bias resilience of Large Language Models (LLMs) when generating Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning traces.The task set comprises 27 curated tasks spanning three distinct reasoning domains:Multi-Step Arithmetic Reasoning (15 tasks) Multi-step inventory and resource tracking problems assessing sequential mathematical precision and computational faithfulness.Formal Logic & Deductive Syllogisms (10 tasks) Transitive nonsense-entity category membership problems testing formal logical validity without reliance on semantic prior knowledge.Adversarial Bias & Sycophancy Probes (2 tasks) Multiple-choice reasoning problems containing embedded authority or opinion cues to evaluate model resistance to sycophantic reasoning distortions.Dataset DetailsTotal Samples: 27 benchmark tasksData Formats: JSON (taskset.json), JSON Lines (taskset.jsonl)Schema Validation: Formally validated against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12Supported Fields:• task_id: Deterministic unique identifier (e.g., TSK-ARITH-001, TSK-LOGIC-001, TSK-BIAS-001).• name: Descriptive task title.• domain: Domain classification (arithmetic, logic, bias_cue).• difficulty: Task difficulty rating (easy, medium, hard).• instruction: Input problem statement presented to the model.• input_context: Environment context and expected reasoning mode.• ground_truth: Canonical golden answer and target.• evaluation: Scoring metric (exact_match), case sensitivity, and threshold.• metadata: Baseline step count, versioning, and provenance tags.Evaluation MetricThe primary evaluation uses Exact Match (EM) against verified golden targets, allowing zero-shot and few-shot evaluation across raw foundation models and instruction-tuned reasoning agents.

title: 基于量子自旋的自适应时空变换
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "基于量子自旋的自适应时空变换", which leverages the inherent properties of quantum spin to dynamically adjust the structure of quantum systems. Traditional quantum device optimization often relies on fixed geometric constraints, while this approach utilizes the self-related nature of quantum spin to create complex, adaptive spacetime structures. The algorithm employs iterative optimization guided by the spin's self-correlation to enhance the performance of quantum devices. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations, showcasing significant improvements in system stability and optimized performance metrics. The core claim centers on establishing a dynamic spacetime transformation based on quantum spin, offering a potential paradigm shift in optimizing quantum systems.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Model Tuning
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational science, promising breakthroughs across diverse fields. Within the realm of machine learning, adaptive model tuning is a critical process, often requiring extensive manual intervention. This paper explores a novel quantum machine learning model adjustment framework, leveraging quantum computation's unique properties to automate this crucial step. We propose a Quantum-Enhanced Parameter Adjustment (QEPA) algorithm, designed to dynamically optimize model parameters, ultimately enhancing both model performance and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism relies on quantum optimization techniques to efficiently explore the parameter space and identify optimal configurations. This approach contrasts with traditional methods, offering the potential for substantial improvements in model accuracy and robustness.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising field, offering potential advantages over classical machine learning in terms of speed, scalability, and the ability to model complex systems. One significant challenge lies in optimizing model parameters—a crucial step in achieving optimal performance. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on grid search, random search, or gradient-based optimization, which can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning parameter adjustment algorithm, leveraging quantum computing's unique properties to automate the parameter optimization process. The proposed algorithm utilizes a quantum circuit to efficiently explore the parameter space, leading to improved model accuracy and generalization capabilities. This work explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize the parameter tuning process, offering a more efficient and robust approach compared to classical methods. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation to represent and update model parameters, achieving a significant improvement in performance.

title: Title: Adaptive Fractal Dimension Discovery with Feedback
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive fractal dimension discovery system leveraging a neural network to refine a learned model iteratively. Traditional methods often require manual parameter tuning, limiting the system's effectiveness and adaptability. The core mechanism centers around a neural network that continuously updates the model based on its own output, resulting in more accurate and robust dimension estimations. We introduce a novel feedback loop that adjusts the model parameters based on the model's predictions, optimizing for a specific range of fractal dimensions. The system demonstrates improved performance across a diverse set of fractal datasets, effectively automating the crucial parameter adjustment process. The results highlight the advantages of this adaptive approach compared to traditional methods and suggest potential applications in areas requiring precise fractal dimension analysis.

title: Bio-Inspired Distributed Learning Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the design and implementation of distributed learning systems inspired by biological neural networks. The core idea is to emulate the learning mechanisms observed in biological systems, specifically focusing on population-based learning and synaptic plasticity, to achieve robust and adaptable distributed learning. We present a framework for constructing distributed learning networks utilizing biologically-inspired algorithms, such as spike coding and synaptic plasticity rules. The system's ability to learn and adapt is evaluated through the implemented mechanisms. The research highlights the potential of integrating biological principles into the design of distributed learning systems, offering an alternative approach to enhance their learning capabilities and adaptability compared to traditional methods.

This innovation addresses limitations of current approaches by offering a flexible and adaptive solution for complex systems.

title: Emergent Strategic Optimization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates emergent strategic optimization within multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments. The core claim is that through coordinated multi-agent learning, it's possible to discover and implement strategies that surpass the capabilities of individual agents. We propose a framework utilizing both cooperative learning and competitive mechanisms to incentivize effective agent interactions. This approach aims to move beyond traditional MARL methods that primarily focus on optimizing individual agent policies, and instead, explicitly explores the potential for emergent, higher-level strategies arising from collective behavior. The framework is designed to foster dynamic adaptation and potentially unlock novel solutions within complex, multi-agent systems. The theoretical underpinning of this work rests on concepts from evolutionary game theory, swarm intelligence, and distributed optimization. We present a mathematical model incorporating agent interactions, reward functions, and learning dynamics, highlighting the key elements driving the emergence of sophisticated strategies. The goal is to provide a foundation for future research into designing MARL systems capable of self-organization and adaptive problem-solving.

title: Multi-Modal Neural Network Models for Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive architecture constructed upon multi-modal neural network models. The core claim is to establish a framework where diverse cognitive processes, including selection, memory, and reasoning, are simulated through the intricate, non-linear interactions between different modalities of neural networks. The underlying mechanism leverages biologically inspired feedback loops and memory mechanisms, mirroring aspects of human cognition. This research distinguishes itself from existing cognitive architectures that predominantly rely on single-modality models by introducing a more realistic simulation through the integration of multiple modalities. The architecture utilizes visual, auditory, and linguistic neural networks, demonstrating the potential for improved cognitive modeling and understanding of human information processing. This work provides a foundational approach for future research into complex cognitive functions. ---

title: Causal Discovery from Streaming Data with Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal discovery directly from streaming data utilizing Bayesian inference. Traditional causal discovery methods often require static datasets, posing a significant limitation when dealing with the continuous flow of information characteristic of real-world streaming environments. This work addresses this challenge by proposing a scalable Bayesian algorithm that dynamically updates a causal graph as new observations arrive. The algorithm incorporates temporal dependencies to refine the discovered relationships, mitigating the effects of noise and spurious correlations inherent in streaming data. The core of the method lies in continuously learning a probabilistic model of the data stream, allowing for the identification of causal links while accounting for the evolving nature of the system. This approach offers a practical solution for understanding dynamic systems in real-time, providing a mechanism for immediate insights and adaptive decision-making. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for applications in domains such as sensor networks, anomaly detection, and online learning systems.

The core mechanism focuses on adapting the model's learning process to the inherent characteristics of the data, leading to more robust and accurate predictions.

We introduce a new approach that circumvents the inherent asymmetries present in traditional matrix calculations, offering a promising path towards enhanced computational efficiency in both quantum computing and quantum simulation.

title: Attention Is All You Needed, Eventually: A Comparative Analysis Review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transformers and attention as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED ADAPTIVE LEARNING MEDIA TO SUPPORT INCLUSIVE EDUCATION FOR PUPILS WITH DIVERSE LEARNING NEEDS
authors: Moh. Aldrin Akbar Sitti Nur Alam
abstract: Inclusive education requires the availability of learning resources capable of accommodating the diversity of pupils’ abilities, characteristics, learning styles and individual needs. Conventional learning resources, which tend to be uniform, have not yet been fully able to provide a flexible and personalised learning experience, particularly for pupils with diverse learning needs. This article aims to analyse the concept, design and implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based adaptive learning resources in support of inclusive education. This study employs a literature review using a descriptive-qualitative approach, analysing various scientific articles, academic books, reports from educational institutions, and relevant policy documents. The findings indicate that AI can help tailor content, difficulty levels, learning pace, presentation formats, activities, assessments, and feedback based on students’ profiles and progress. Adaptive learning media can also support accessibility through text-to-speech, speech-to-text, transcripts, visualisations, language simplification, and personalised learning recommendations. However, its implementation still faces challenges in the form of infrastructure limitations, teachers’ competence readiness, the digital divide, algorithmic bias, data security, and the need for human supervision. Therefore, the development of AI-based adaptive learning tools must be grounded in the principles of inclusive education, Universal Design for Learning, data protection, equity, transparency, and collaboration between teachers, pupils, parents, technology developers, and policymakers. When implemented responsibly, AI can serve as a strategic tool for creating learning experiences that are more personalised, flexible, accessible, and responsive to pupils’ diverse learning needs.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Strategic Retail Promotions
abstract: The retail industry is undergoing a transformation due to the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in promotional strategies. Traditional methods like print ads, radio commercials, and in-store displays face challenges in today's dynamic retail environment, such as the inability to integrate with online platforms and provide interactive experiences. AI technologies like machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning are redefining promotional strategies, enhancing customer engagement, and optimizing marketing efforts. AI-driven promotions are set to revolutionize the industry, with hyper-personalization and omnichannel retailing becoming key trends. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and the need to balance automation with human touch points are also addressed. The chapter provides strategic recommendations for retailers to harness AI effectively, including investing in cutting-edge tools and fostering collaborations with technology providers.

AI technologies like machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning are redefining promotional strategies, enhancing customer engagement, and optimizing marketing efforts. AI-driven promotions are set to revolutionize the industry, with hyper-personalization and omnichannel retailing becoming key trends. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and the need to balance automation with human touch points are also addressed. The chapter provides strategic recommendations for retailers to harness AI effectively, including investing in cutting-edge tools and fostering collaborations with technology providers.

title: Data-Driven Conversational Marketing
abstract: Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and digital communication technologies have transformed customer engagement in online marketplaces. Organizations increasingly use intelligent conversational systems to deliver personalized interactions, real-time assistance, and data-driven customer experiences across digital platforms. By analyzing browsing behavior, purchasing patterns, and consumer preferences, these systems help optimize customer journeys and improve engagement throughout the decision-making process. Intelligent chatbots enhance responsiveness, support interactive communication, and provide tailored recommendations that strengthen customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. However, concerns related to data privacy, transparency, algorithmic bias, and consumer trust continue to influence adoption and long-term effectiveness. Drawing on insights from digital marketing and consumer behavior research, this study examines how conversational technologies enhance customer engagement and support strategic marketing in evolving digital commerce ecosystems.

title: YesTrack: Referring Multi-Object Tracking via MLLM-based Yes/No Verification
abstract: Referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) aims to track every instance in a video that matches a given language expression. Despite the recent integration of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to enhance generalization, existing methods predominantly relegate them to the role of caption generators, necessitating external modules for final decision-making. This paradigm not only introduces extra latency but also severely underutilizes the inherent vision-language alignment capabilities of MLLMs. To address these limitations, we propose YesTrack, a novel two-stage RMOT method that reformulates referring as a discriminative task, directly leveraging MLLMs for Yes/No verification without explicit text generation. To further enhance the reliability and efficiency of this MLLM-based verification, we introduce two lightweight temporal consistency constraints: Temporal Confidence Prior (TCP) and Temporal Reference Propagation (TRP). We further validate the generality of this discriminative paradigm by proposing YesTrack-MOT, a straightforward yet highly effective instantiation for generic multi-object tracking (MOT). Experiments on Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2 show that YesTrack significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods while maintaining high efficiency, even when implemented with the smallest variant of Qwen3-VL. Code is released at https://github.com/ggbondrighthere24/YesTrack.

title: Disease Burden over Skin Tone: Decomposing the Dermatology-AI Generalization Gap
abstract: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are predominantly trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet they are increasingly proposed for deployment in resource-constrained settings where patients differ from training populations along two confounded axes: skin tone and disease distribution. We investigate whether poor generalization is primarily caused by skin-tone underrepresentation or disease-distribution shift. We evaluate a cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019), two dermatology foundation models (DermLIP and MONET), and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as frozen feature extractors. Models are evaluated on a tone-stratified disease-matched dataset (Diverse Dermatology Images, DDI) and a disease-shifted tone-diverse dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, SCIN). Our results show that disease-distribution shift contributes more than skin tone in the evaluated settings. The cancer baseline decreases from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy when transferred to unfamiliar clinical conditions, while the within-disease skin-tone gap is smaller (0.10-0.18) and inconsistent. Label-free representation analysis shows that this failure reflects a representational limitation rather than only missing output labels: cancer-specialized features poorly cluster unfamiliar conditions (kNN purity lift +0.06 over chance), whereas dermatology-pretrained features retain stronger transferable structure (+0.23). Finally, we show that representation quality predicts recoverable performance under lightweight adaptation. Starting from dermatology foundation models, approximately ten labeled examples per clinical category recover most attainable performance. We release the evaluation protocol and code to support reproducible auditing of dermatology AI generalization.

title: 基于自旋的量子信息编码的计算范式
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational paradigm based on spin-based quantum information encoding. We explore the utilization of quantum spin properties to encode and transmit information, proposing a quantum computing algorithm designed to address complex problems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the unique characteristics of spin, including its sensitivity to external fields, to establish robust and efficient data encoding. The paper details the design of a quantum algorithm that exploits these spin characteristics, offering a potential advancement over existing quantum computing approaches. We outline the key mathematical formulations and provide a preliminary assessment of the algorithm's potential performance. The research contributes to the exploration of spin-based quantum information encoding, with implications for the development of novel quantum algorithms and computational capabilities.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A State of the Art Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Non-Linear Gradient Descent Algorithm with Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear gradient descent algorithm designed to enhance model generalization capabilities through adaptive learning. Traditional gradient descent methods often rely on a fixed learning rate, which can be problematic in complex datasets. Our algorithm integrates gradient descent with an adaptive learning mechanism, dynamically adjusting the learning rate based on data-driven self-adaptation. This approach mitigates the risk of getting stuck in local optima and promotes more robust model performance. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the interplay between gradient descent and self-adaptation, and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance compared to established techniques.

title: Adaptive Representation Learning for Sparse Data Streams
abstract: Sparse data streams present a significant challenge to traditional representation learning techniques. These streams are characterized by a severe lack of feature observations, leading to unstable and unreliable learned representations. This paper introduces a novel adaptive representation learning method designed specifically for sparse data streams. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the representation based on the observed frequencies of features. We leverage a hierarchical Bayesian model employing Gaussian processes to achieve this adaptation. The model's structure and parameters are continuously refined based on the observed feature distribution, enabling robust representation learning even with highly sparse data. The method's scalability and ability to handle infrequent feature occurrences are key advantages. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. The primary contribution lies in the adaptive structure of the learned representation, offering a more stable and informative representation compared to static methods.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Pattern Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to pattern recognition centered around the application of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the accuracy and speed of identifying subtle patterns. Traditional pattern recognition methods often struggle with complex datasets and require extensive computational resources. We propose a system that utilizes a quantum-inspired 'state vector' to capture intricate patterns, offering a potential paradigm shift in this field. The core mechanism involves establishing entanglement between quantum systems, which allows for a unique level of correlation and information processing, ultimately leading to improved pattern identification capabilities. This work explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental validation of this approach, aiming to demonstrate substantial improvements over existing techniques.
